body:
Franchement je les ai toutes essayées. Les gratuites, les payantes. Il n’y a pas photo, les gars de CultureCode on pensé à (quasiment) tout !
L’application de gestion de tâches la plus complète et le plus intuitive a ce jour.  
Point barre.
author: Corto Maltese 92

title: Excellente application
body: Superbe application très utile que ce soit pour les tâches quotidiennes ou les projets à long terme! Et en lus elle est très belle... Bravo
author: Pacaale

title: Le top du top !
body: Cette application est vraiment le must pour l’organisation, je ne regrette pas mon achat
author: Jordan42x

title: Déçu
body:
Beaucoup de mal à comprendre l’engouement pour cette application.
À plus de 10 euros pour la gestion des tâches, je m’attendais au produit parfait.
C’est plutôt l’inverse...
Pas de gestion des tâches Exchange, pas de possibilité de mettre un rappel (notification) à un jour différent de la tâche et Siri qui ne reconnaît absolument jamais l’instruction d’ajout. 
Bref, passé l’interface très épurée et claire, c’est une grosse régression par rapport à ma précédente application 😒
author: tuyau86

title: Application au TOP !
body: Il y a « Things 3 » et il y a toutes les autres applications d’organisation ! Things est honnêtement loin devant les autres ! Certes assez chère mais finalement quand on voit tout ce qu’on peut faire avec, le prix me paraît convenable ! Merci à « Things 3 » qui change mon organisation dans ma vie privée mais surtout dans ma vie professionnelle !
author: Clement62360

title: Une vrai logique d’organisation
body: J’ai vraiment l’impression que je ne vais rien oublier et j’ai trouvé un support efficace pour “Getting Things Done” et “Les 7 habitudes”
author: Morse15

title: Très jolie app de gestion de tâches

Belle mise à jour de design !

author: François Bourdoncle

title: Meilleure appli d'organisation
body:
Top ! Très pratique et très intuitive !
Je suis fan

title: Excellent
body: On découvre au fur et à mesure toute la puissance de cette application que ce soit sur le fond comme sur les détails. Bravo.
author: iFlyingphil

title: Super
body:
Application facile à utiliser et connecté à ma montre
Je trouve dommage de pas pouvoir aussi noter l'heure des Rdv c pour cela que je ne mets pas 5*
author: Tanseb

title: Surpris
body: J'étais un peu inquiet de devoir dépenser une somme non négligeable pour une application qui dans sa précédente version ne m'avait pas tout à fait conquis. Mais à l'usage je ne regrette pas l'investissement sur mes trois supports (iPhone, iPad et MacBook). Les changements sont réellement positifs et vont dans le sens de la souplesse et de l'adaptabilité. Ce n'est pas la perfection, mais tel quel j'avoue en être extrêment satisfait.
author: Arvoitus

title: Agréable
body: Très agréable à utiliser. Je la conseille.
author: El Padré 974

title: Très efficace, rapide, simple
body: Excellent gestionnaire de choses à faire avec partage depuis les emails. Souple à l'usage. Parmi toutes les alternatives nombreuses sur le marché, c'est celui que j'ai fini par adopter.
author: jacmichel

title: Excellent.
body: Meilleur app d'organisation, je ne met pas 5 étoile car elle est très chère et il faut re payer pour l'avoir sur Mac malheureusement !
author: Loicb230310

title: Bien, chère, idée ajout
body:
Très bonne appli, un peu regrettable de devoir la racheter sur chaque support, pas de version iPad Pro, pas de vrai rappel, le système de datage n'est pas assez approfondi. J'aimerais pouvoir recevoir des notifications à chaque heure à laquelle je dois exécuter une tâche. De sorte à ne pas avoir besoin de me rappeler qu'il faut que j'aille sur l'application afin qu'elle me rappelle ce que je dois faire...
À part cela, c'est très bien!

Édit du 1er juillet: j'ai beaucoup aimé utilisé cette application, surtout pour se lancer dans une quête de productivité. Excellente pour se lancer, on prend beaucoup de plaisir à pouvoir cocher les objectifs que l'on s'est fixé. J'ai commencé à m'en servir de plus en plus jusqu'à finalement en découvrir les limites, ce qui me pousse à changer d'application pour l'instant. En tout cas je la recommande, elle mérite bien un 4 étoiles pour un publique qui cherche avant tout une bonne première appli, même si elle est un peu chère. Dans le meilleur des cas ce sera une raison pour se forcer à l'utiliser.
author: kanerame

title: Super application
body: Très bonne application dommage qu'il faille payer pour l'application iPad ce qui rend le total élevé. Une 5e étoile avec une nouvelle politique de prix.
author: jph43

title: Chère, mais vraiment bien faite
body:
Si on met de côté le prix, surtout si on veux l'appli, sur ordi, sur iPhone et sur ipad (je n'ai pas pris ce dernier), l'application est vraiment au dessus des autres. Bravo aux développeurs. 
On se focalise sur les tâches proches, et les tâches éloignées, ne viennent pas polluées l'écran. 
J'ai énormément de tâches récurrentes et vraiment c'est très bien fait. 

Je ne regrette pas mon achat.
author: Stmalot

title: La version que j'attendais depuis des années.
body: Une étoile en moins car malgré tout trop chère. Surtout lorsque qu'on achète aussi la version Mac et iPad.
author: Norman06460

title: Ne vaut pas tripette
body:
Interface  pénible en particulier pour les rappel horaire . Classification obscure. Pas de rappel geotagué. Pas de délégation de tâche.
Trois appli pour mes machines (phone,pad,Mac). 
J'ai misé 10€ pour voir... c'est tout vu et pour tous dire déjà effacé.
author: kiju

title: Tip top
body:
All I needed - Simple, ergonomic, efficient
Definitely helped improving my productivity
author: Luinn

title: Cher mais assez parfait
body:
J'ai beaucoup hésité, j'avais peur que cette application ne me convienne pas, sachant que j'en ai un usage particulier.
J'ai finalement craqué et j'ai bien fait, cette App est franchement parfaite, jolie, rapide, ergonomique et suffisamment flexible pour pouvoir l'utiliser à sa façon.
Un must !

title: Magnifique
body: Très bon logiciel !!
author: Xxl971

body: Thank you!

title: Parfait ! Mais...
body:
L'application est top sur tous les points : 
- productivité 
- ergonomie 
- multiplateforme 
En revanche elle ne fait tjs pas vaut tâches pour vous !
author: Etiem

title: Vraiment pas cool la trilogie de prix !
body:
Utilisateur de la version 2 sur Mac, iPad et iPhone, cette fois-ci, devant le prix de chaque version (il y en a trois), j'ai renoncé à acquérir celle de l'iPad !
La pseudo "prime" à la fidélité étant particulièrement mesquine, car accessible même aux primo-acheteurs 😡...

Ce sera donc pour moi le début de la fin avec cette appli, car je n'envisage pas une solution de se type qui ne soit pas synchro sur mes trois appareils.

Franchement, un seul Things 3 compatible iPhone/iPad comme le font beaucoup d'autres éditeurs aurait fait un peu moins "tir aux pigeons" surtout aux prix exigé.
Et bien sur la version 3 étant incompatible avec la version 2, impossible de synchroniser mon iPad avec les 2 autres.
Bien vu ! 😤
Dommage cette politique, car elle tue l'intérêt d'un produit pourtant bien réussi !

Adieu, donc à Cultured code ... 😥
author: webscan

title: Maginigique, simple et efficace.
body:
Je recherchais une application pour gérer mes tâches personnelles, longtemps utilisateurs de l'application native "Rappels", celle-ci me laisser quelques peu sur ma faim.
Avant de me décider à acheter Things 3 j'ai réfléchi à cause du prix qui est certes élevé mais mérité au final.
L'application est magnifique, épurée, simple utilisation tout en étant extrêmement complète. La synchronisation est juste parfaite avec mon Mac !

Bravo aux développeurs pour le travail réalisé et j'espère qu'il y aura les mises à jour régulières.
author: Yoskiz

title: So great
body: Love love love this new version!!!
author: silvtal

title: Retour en grâce
body: Utilisateur de Things 2, j'avais délaissé une application moribonde pour me tourner vers Todoist qui correspondait plus à mon usage. Things 3 m'a fait revenir à mes premières amours. Certes, c'est cher à l'achat mais on ne paye qu'une et une seule fois. Mais, même s'il me manque (encore) quelques fonctionnalités, le design et l'expérience utilisateur incomparables m'ont fait définitivement oublier ma passade Todoist. Things 3 est puissant, simple, et totalement intégré à l'univers Apple. Kudos to Cultured Code ! 😘
author: BoscuMunin

title: Formidable !
body: J'utilise Things 3 pour la première fois, et pour moi qui ai de gros pbs d'organisation, c'est génial ! Prise en main et utilisation facile, ça me change la vie !
author: Madame Turquoise

title: Très belle évolution
body: L'outil est moderne et élégant. Intuitif et beaucoup simple d'emploi que la version précédente. Cela valait le coût d'attendre même si ce fut long...
author: --Obi1--

title: Appli très efficace
body: Ce que j'aime dans cette application est sa réduction au stricte nécessaire sans rien oublier : un raccourci efficace pour saisir une nouvelle note depuis n'importe quel environnement (et on peut même attacher des mails, documents etc. !), étiquettes, lien avec rappels iOS etc. La nouvelle interface est très agréable et sans "poudre aux yeux" histoire de faire semblant… la seule chose qui manque est l'aspect collaboratif. Bravo !
author: Reuter68

title: Fan-tas-tique!
body:
Cette nouvelle version de Things est vraiment fantastique!
Le design simple et super joli, la typo super claire et belle, les interactions et animations qui apportent une super ergonomie...
Beaucoup diront que l'app (et ses déclinaisons Mac, iPhone, iPad) est chère, mais ça vaut vraiment le coup. Je m'en sers toute la journée, tous les jours, pour le boulot et le perso, et c'est un réel plaisir!
author: SkyNebula

title: Simplement la meilleure
body: J'utilise Things quotidiennement depuis plusieurs années maintenant sur iPhone et Mac, cette nouvelle version apporte des améliorations à une appli déjà excellente.
author: Balic

title: Très fonctionnel !
body: Vraiment pratique et simple d'utilisation. Aucune idée ne se perd !
author: CigarAddict

title: Parfait
body:
Nouvelle interface tres sympa. Me manque juste la fonction "faire apparaître dans aujourd'hui" 
Sinon super apps même si un peu chère.
author: gdpe

title: La version 2 etait bien, la version 3, par sa simplicité,  m'est devenue indispensable
body: Vraiment chouette, bien intégrée avec d'autres applis tel calendar, les quick entrys etc....
author: Inivosirob

body: Mon appli préférée. Je l'utilise tous les jours depuis des années et je ne peux plus m'en passer. Aussi, le nouveau design est magnifique 😉
author: JJeedy

title: Excellent
body: De la ort d'un estoy adopter !
author: M PERRY

title: Ça fait le taff !
body: Très bonne application. Par contre je ne comprends pas pourquoi l'app macOS est plus de 40€ ?! Surtout si il y a les mêmes fonctionnalités que sur iOS !
author: Louis3741

title: Sobre et efficace
body: Je suis fan. J'ai un peu tiqué en voyant le prix (je n'avais acheté la version 2 que quelques mois auparavant) mais c'est la seule application hors Apple à être dans ma barre d'accès rapide et je m'en sers tous les jours. Toutes les améliorations sont logiques et apporte un plus appréciable. Pas de regrets pour ma part.
author: Actorios

title: Enfin !
body:
J'attendais avec impatience une nouvelle version pour passer à la caisse, et je ne suis pas déçu ! Pour l'instant le pari est gagné, ultra simple d'utilisation mais avec beaucoup de fonctions cachés.
Espérant qu'il y aura de belles mises à jour à venir !
author: tomcdl

title: Exceptionnel
body: Le niveau du détail est ici amené au plus extrême. Tout, absolument tout, est réfléchi avec soin.
author: LudovicLoridan

title: Bravo ! Continuez !
body: Je viens de revenir à cette application dans sa dernière version, magnifique design et superbes fonctionnalités. Merci.
author: hangloose59

title: Exceptional
body:
I'm a longtime user, and every change in v3 is a clear and deliberate improvement. I happily paid to update for Mac and iPhone, it's much much better.
Note that this is not compatible with Things 2, but you CAN switch back to v2, your data will be the same as before you switched to v3 (I tested it).
author: Potatoihave

title: Efficace, ergonomique
body: Cette nouvelle version prolonge l'esprit de la précédente : pratique, fiable, bien faite... logiciel un peu cher peut-être, en mettant bout à bout le prix des versions iPhone, iPad et Mac.
author: pmontel

title: Une redécouverte
body: Dirigeant de société, je redécouvre dans Things un outil précieux qui permet de structurer et organiser la masse de données et d'informations d'une gestion structurée de projet
author: Jean-Louis 96

title: Antistress
body: Pensé pour ne pas stresser, très agréable.
author: Jojolipo

title: Excellent update
body:
Vraiment plus intuitif que la version 2.
Je l'utilise en application de la méthode GTD et je suis très satisfait.
author: Yann Jaigu

title: Sublime et efficace
body: J'ai cette app depuis leur toute première version. Je viens de télécharger la version 3 qui s'est fait attendre plusieurs années, et bien cela fait bizarre de le dire mais l'attente en valait vraiment la peine ! Incroyable travail effectué par l'équipe.
author: nclairembault

title: De tres belle améliorations
body: Vraiment bien pensé le système de projet, sous-tâches. Belle ergonomie par rapport à la version 2. Mais à ce tarif le système de rappel est risible quand on voie ce que fait Due, de plus un accès web pour pouvoir utiliser Things du bureau (windows) aurait été appréciable.

title: Top

body:
Bof, sans doute puissant, mais je ne suis pas sur qu'il corresponde à mes besoins. 
L'application d'origine me convient bien. 
Appli cher, proposer une version d'essai limitée serait plus honnête... je n'aurais sans doute pas acheté.
author: GHED

title: J'adore depuis le début
body:
J'utilise cette application sur mon Mac et mon iPhone depuis qu'elle existe. J'en suis très satisfait. Elle est tout à fait adapté à mon utilisation. Je gère le système informatique d'un groupement de laboratoire d'analyses.
J'ai parfois été tenté d'essayer d'autres applications gratuites. Mais toujours je reviens à Things.
author: Agalujie

title: Très bien
body: La force de Things à toujours été sa simplicité et sa fiabilité, donc son efficacité. Quoi de plus naturel que de classer ses tâches par ordre de réalisation dans la journée ? J'avais peur que cultured code "se perde" avec cette version 3 et tombe dans du GTD pur et dur à la Omnifocus avec une usine à gaz que l'on fini par ne plus utiliser. Il n'en est rien. Cette version garde toute la philosophie de things2, mais puissance 10. Je ne comprend pas ceux qui achètent et viennent mal noter parce qu'il faut payer, les développeurs ne vivent pas d'amour et d'eau fraîche.....
author: Jeffo13

title: Indispensable
body:
Je l'utilise depuis l'origine, sur iPhone et iPad. Et mon épouse idem. 
La V3 est un rafraîchissement sympathique, avec encore plus de souplesse.
Le prix reste abordable pour le service rendu, car je m'en sers tous les jours.
Par contre, je laisse tomber la version Mac, que nous utilisions qu'occasionnellement.

title: Indispensable et ergonomique !
body:
L'icône est restée la même par rapport à Things 2, mais tout le reste est nouveau et repensé. L'app est très agréable à utiliser, très belle et très moderne. Pour moi elle est indispensable grâce à ses fonctions de rappels récurrents, auxquels s'ajoute maintenant un très astucieux horodatage des tâches qui est facultatif - il n'apparaît que quand on en a besoin !

Bref ce sont des magiciens les développeurs de cette app, elle est très 
 bien conçue.

author: GetLoose17

body:
J'ai teSte beaucoup d'application de tâche ... mais j'ai enfin trouvé Celle dont j'avais besoin: épurée, efficace ... Joli travail 

Reste des options à rajouter pour être parfaite...
author: Joff33

title: La meilleure application pour le GTD sur Mac et iOS
body:
Merci à Cultured Code pour cette magnifique mise à jour!

Cette application allie depuis le début l'élégance et la sobriété de son interface à une gestion des tâches très robuste et complète. 

Je suis utilisateur de longue date, et ayant essayé la plupart des applications concurrentes je suis toujours revenu vers Things qui me convient parfaitement. 
Les quelques fonctions qui pouvaient me manquer dans la version 2 ont été ajoutées dans cette mise à jour (notifications, visualisation du calendrier dans l'application...) et même plus!

Cela valait vraiment la peine d'attendre et je ne regrette pas un seul centime de mes achats (Mac/iPad/iPhone). 

Encore bravo à Cultured Code pour leur travail!
author: SynopticAce

title: Déçu de mon achat des les premières minutes.
body:
Sur le papier c'est application paraît être un bon choix...
Avec la gestion ztd / gtd
Mais dès les premières minutes d'utilisation nous pouvons déjà constaté les points non aboutis...
Calendrier, affichage,…

Pour le prix je m'attendais à avoir beaucoup plus de possibilités de modification et de personnalisation.

Je demande des maintenant le remboursement auprès d'Apple.

Je continue pour ma part avec any.do qui reste une application vraiment très très bien, même en version gratuite.

Peut-être avec la version 4 ?
author: DLEMAPPLE

title: Excellent !
body: Je suis un utilisateur de Todo List très exigeant. Là ... je suis impressionné par la fluidité et l'efficacité de cette application. Bravo et merci pour votre beau travail !

author: gerald85

title: Excellent
body:
Cette appli est vraiment excellente depuis les premières versions, celle-ci apporte son lot d'améliorations tant visuelles et ergonomiques que sous le capot.
Félicitations à toutes l'équipe pour ce travail magnifique.

Une seule remarque 🙂 le mode paysage n'est pas supporté, sur un iPhone 7 Plus c'est un peu dommage...
author: Tippit74

title: Shared projects please !!
body:
Amazing app, design and interactions are excellent.

A bit expensive but it's important to sustain small developers.

Things only misses one feature to be a must have IMO : shared projects. Hope we'll see this in a future update 🤞

author: Karakine01

title: The best GTD app for Robinson Crusoe
body:
This app is very well designed, with a beautiful and handy interface. But Things only does half of the basics in task management. It's like your alone on a desert island with nobody around: 
1) no task assignment to somebody else (even if you don't actually assign a task to somebody else, you may want to track what you are expecting from others)
2) no list sharing (to bad if you and your wife - or husband - are going to the grocery store and get 2 times a pack of 6x bottles of milk, or on the opposite you thought she or he would have bought the toilet papers that was dramatically missing at home... you got the idea)
... for the most required functionality.
And 3) unfortunately geo-tagged reminder is not available whereas iOS offers this great opportunity. But no need, Robinson has washed up on a so small island.
author: JohnRowland

title: Perfectible.
body:
Cette nouvelle interface est pas mal mais je dois admettre qu'il y a quelques points de détail qui me chagrinent :

- Il manque l'impossibilité de masquer les projets sous le nom de domaine, de fait l'écran d'accueil est vite plein quand on a de nombreux projets en cours et ça peut être décourageant.

- Les projets "Un jour" qu'on aimerait bien masquer apparaissent... tout en haut de la liste des projets en cours. Impossible de les déplacer en bas. Par ailleurs ils apparaissent 2 fois (une fois dans la boite "Un jour" et une fois dans la liste "projets pour plus tard", ce qui est inutile et perturbant.

Pour une app qui passe du gratuit au payant j'aurais aimé un peu plus de professionnalisme...

title: Un must

L'intégration du calendrier est géniale, l'app est magnifique. Plein de petites améliorations par-ci par par-là. Si vous trouvez que l'app est chère: la version précédente de Things a été mise à jour gratuitement pendant plusieurs années, l'app est vraiment de grande qualité tout comme le support. En un mot: génial.

title: Feature request
body: Things is great, theirs no getting away from the fact, it’s very nearly perfect. For me perfection would be complete if only the Devs would add some sounds! Every other app of this genre has sounds, but “things” the best of the lot has absolutely nothing. No sounds to pick for alerts, no sound to complete a task, or mark off a check box, no animations, no nothing. Please Devs do all us near sighted old boys (and Gals) a favour, add some sounds so we know we’re on the right track. Other then that, thanks for a near perfect app.

author: l i a m 0 1

title: Old timer with some ideas
body:
I'm a user of Things since version 1 and a product designer. I've seen how many technologies have changed over time, and what happens when industry leaders get lazy.

Things is still an amazing app for productivity — it’s position in many country’s App Stores proves this. Meanwhile, many competing apps now feature collaboration, AI-integration, and other improvements.

Things needs to integrate these features now, while they’re still in the lead; otherwise, competitors with these features will eventually take over.

As Steve Jobs said, “Innovation distinguishes between a leader and a follower.”
author: Joshua Kaufman

title: The perfect productivity app
body: I’ve been using Things 3 for years and it’s brilliant. I love how it’s calm and free of visual clutter - other to-do apps just stress me out with all the colour choices and other unnecessary things. I also love that I can view my calendar events in Things without them becoming tasks which is the perfect way to do it. This app is brilliant and the recent updates to repeating tasks are just the icing on the cake.

author: Funkyjui1ce

title: Ok but nothing more
body:
I’ve had the app almost three weeks and it’s ok but I’m not impressed. 

It’s not at all intuitive to use, particularly if you use repeating tasks. Getting started with the system is a frustrating experience and given the functionality or lack of it, not worth the hassle. 

The different options to input repeating tasks aren’t at all clear and why you should use one or the other. It’s easy to end up with multiple entries for the same task. 

If you want to get back to zero so you can try setting it up again it’s a complicated multi step process without instructions. 

When you do have it set up it’s hard to understand why the app works in a particular way and going the help pages really doesn’t help a whole lot. 

For me, it’s not been worth it and I’ll be going back to my old app.
author: Jentious2000

title: A very beautiful app, with one major oversight that makes it unusable (for me)
body:
I think Things 3 is mostly fine. It’s very pretty, simple and, on the face of it, can do everything a modern task manager needs to do. But it has one major flaw that means I can’t use it. 

For some unknown reason (clear only to Cultured Code) users cannot use natural language to create a task. I want to write “do the thing at 8pm” and for it to create a reminder called “do the thing” with a reminder set for 8pm. But things won’t add the reminder. Instead, it will name the task “do the thing at 8pm” and then I’ll have to manually set the time and date. 

Most other apps are capable of doing it, so why not this one? 

I’m sure someone will say it’s the “purists” choice, and means we have to be more intentional in our task management, blah, blah, blah…but that’s just an excuse for poor UX. 

It is a maddening design choice and I cannot think of any reason what’s why it is not possible in this app. 

Such a shame.
author: Troffers

title: Don’t change a Thing(s)
body: I’ve been using Things 3 now daily for the past 5+ years, for iPhone and Mac. It’s by far the best third party app I use. It’s so well considered from a product standpoint. body: Things feels powerful but never overwhelming. It balances structure with simplicity, which is exactly what I need to juggle creative work, academic responsibilities, and life admin. author: ben_mw

title: The best on the market, but could still be better
body:
In many ways a superb app, but my main gripe is the lack of a ‘Time’ concept, both for scheduling and deadline purposes. 

I understand that this is an uncritical implementation of ‘Getting Things Done’ methodology. But I would argue that GTD philosophy is flawed, and that in practice, this uncritical implementation makes for a limited user experience.

Some tasks only become actionable after a certain time of day but can remain actionable for days or even months thereafter. For example: I will only be able to book something for a non-specific date after I finish speaking to Person A at midday today, so don’t want this task surfaced to me as actionable this morning whilst I’m commuting to meet them.

Others tasks are actionable from their inception, but ultimately have very specific time deadlines, which would be helpful to see in the user interface, especially as this deadline approaches. For example: I will need to submit a document by 13:00 five months from now, and because it won’t take long to submit I am minded to leave it until much nearer the time because I’ve got a stack of other non-deadlined tasks that I’d like to prioritise. 

Separate to my Time gripe, 
I would value more sophisticated filtering options of my various list views, including the option to filter by tasks that do ‘NOT’ have a certain label attached to them. This would save the proliferation of unnecessary additional filters and lists.

title: Still hands down the best !
body:
Cultured Code are still doing the right thing really well. The app works brilliantly, the updates are incremental and clearly well tested before release and the UI is still as joyful to use as ever. I just wish more developers would use Things3 as a gold standard example for how to do application design supremely well.  I guess if could ask for one thing it would be under the skin e2e encryption 
So.. One of, if not the best example of great user centric design I have ever used.. Clear, fluid, pleasantly interactive and efficient. Looks really nice as well. .. as they say “if it ain’t broke, don’t fix it!” 
Maintains 5* all the way for me :)

title: Life changing
body:
I purchased this app for iPhone and Mac at the start of this year as part of an ongoing attempt to get a handle on my workflow. I work two jobs while pursuing a career in  acting and, as a result, I have a lot of things to do in a lot of different categories at any given time. 

I tried pen and paper but those to do lists are inflexible and time consuming so were never a long term solution. I became dependent on the built in reminders app but this resulted in a single unwieldy list where some items would stay for months at a time. 

‘Things’ is the answer. With this app I can sit down every month or so, decide what I want to get done, make to do lists and then, this is the improtant bit, set a date for each specific ‘to do’. The result is that you wake up every morning with a curated list of what you need to be getting on with which also includes your calendar events for the day. 

Widgets are great, the ui is incredible, the cloud updates in an instant so I can access and edit my lists seamlessly on both devices.

And, best of all, it’s a one off payment. I hate ‘subscribing’ to software and am really pleased ‘things’ doesn’t indulge in this business model. I can’t recommend the app enough.

title: Simple and powerful
body: I never write app reviews but I can’t overstate how happy I am with this product - even with the large (one-off) fee. I’m a GP in the UK and I have multiple work management, home management and learning goals to prioritise and execute (to be clear, this app is NOT suitable for any confidential information and my clinical work is entirely managed within our secure IT system at work). I’ve been looking for a product like this for a long time but was put off by the cost of Things 3 but I followed other reviewers advice and went online to the website and set up a two week free trial. The set-up process took about three hours to capture and organise all my commitments and I felt immensely relieved at the end of it. After a few days, I was convinced enough to buy the product outright. Two weeks later and my brain no longer has obligations rattling around in it and I’m getting through work at a great rate because tasks are already there to do. I tend to look through the ‘Anytime’ folder at the end of the day and schedule some tasks for the next day. I created several areas for different projects and also a ‘waiting for’ area. Highly recommend this product.

title: Pretty good, but the annoyances remain
body:
Annoyances still remain:

 If you accidentally tap or drag the “New Task” button (seems to happen to me a lot) and don’t enter any text, I would expect to be able to tap away and for the task to just not exist. Instead you have to manually delete it.

When you want to set a quick reminder, if you select a time that’s before the time on the current day, then it just ignores you. This is marginally better than when it used to yell at you. But if I want to quickly set a reminder for tomorrow, I need to go into the calendar, pull down, type something vaguely 9 like and then select 9am tomorrow. It’s the most work I’ve ever had to do to use a natural language input. Things should be letting me type once in the task description and detecting stuff like reminder times and deadlines. Please just release Things 4 with these fixes and I’ll happily pay for it.

title: Good but limited
body:
If you want a really simple task organiser, Things3 is great. Although expensive to use on several devices, it has a lovely clean interface, and syncs really well. It’s actually a pleasure to use. 

But … it’s a bit limited, especially if you like to plan ahead. 
When I look at my tasks due Tomorrow, they appear in a completely random order that can’t be changed. 
Apparently applying a basic sort order (e.g. by project!!) has been logged as a feature request. 
But there is no transparency about this — let alone a published development backlog or roadmap. 

After enjoying my experience with Things, I’ll be moving on soon to something a lot more flexible. I wish I’d chosen that route in the first place — it would have saved me a lot of time & money.

title: Brilliant but crying out for new features.
body:
I really do love Things 3, I have it for Mac and iPhone and use everyday. It has been too long since there’s been any significant feature upgrades now, would be great if you shared your roadmap. 

The ability to upload images/files would be super helpful. 

The ability to forward iMessages into the app in the same way as spark emails can be. 

Location based reminders would be a helpful.

A calendar view with time blocking feature would be helpful. (I like that ical inputs pull through) but would be good to see Things inputs alongside iCal inputs on a Things calendar view. 

Moving the move, tag and time/date buttons to the top would save having to scroll to the bottom of a long entry that has been forwarded from email. This is a frustrating UX experience. 

Please give us a clue on what’s being worked on, I’m sure it would result in more sales.

Couple of years later, tried it again and SHOCKED to find nothing seems to have changed. The AppStore blurb still calls it all new except it’s been “all new” for a few years now. Aside from that, still no natural language entry, still no shared lists, no integrations, etc.

title: Fantastic tool, can it do more?

There are some things that I’d love to see come to future versions of the app:
- the ability to add headings within areas, just like you can in projects. This would be really useful to separate out tasks within areas that don’t fall in to a specific project
- expand the ‘Today’ and ‘This Evening’ feature so include ‘This Morning’ and ‘This Afternoon’. This would help to better layout a day of tasks

I can’t fault the app, these are ideas that could take it even further

author: Trenowin

title: Close to perfect with room for improvement
body:
I seldom write reviews on the App Store unless an app is truly exceptional and Things 3 is just one of those apps. Truthfully, if I could I’d give this app 4.5/5 if that were possible, but docking an entire star for the reasons I have feels a bit unfair considering the impact it’s had on my daily life. Perhaps you have reservations about the price tag; I did too but I’m pleased to say it was worth every penny. It’s perhaps the only app that has actually increased my productivity almost instantaneously. I used to use Evernote for my todo list and I noticed that even though I was writing things down, I wasn’t getting them done. Instead they’d just sit there often getting lost as I made newer notes. Because Things is designed to get you completing tasks instead of just writing about them, there are powerful features to support this, such as badges that tell you how many tasks you have for the day when you aren’t in the app, and easy ways of creating new tasks and moving them around. It removes a lot of the anxiety that comes from having a busy day and not knowing what to tackle first. 
That being said, no app is perfect and I have three key suggestions for the developers on where to improve. 

- It would be great if there were some kind of quick swipe action or even a button to quickly move something to tomorrow. 

- Being able to select anytime in the same menu as someday when changing the date of a task would be very useful (currently the only way is to go to search, type anytime, then tap anytime when it comes up, which isn’t very intuitive). 

- Badges show up for everything you have to do today, regardless of whether it set to today or this evening. it would be good if there were a way to add a custom rule to badge count to only display badges based on the time of day (e.g) you have 3 todos today, 4 this evening making 7 in total. Instead of showing 7, there should be an option to show 3, then 4 later.

title: Managing my ADHD through it.
body:

I suspect paying up front for iOS, later adding iPadOS, lately MacOS seems to keep me sticking with it. I‘m chronically indecisive and used to hop from one system to the next.

Catching fleeting thoughts in Inbox and perusing them later is hugely enjoyable, so is organising them.
Ticking off even the tiniest tasks rewards adding them in the first place.

It‘s become my ADHD‘s first beneficial addiction. :)

title: Fantastic app, but…
body:
I do love this app so bought both the macOS and iOS versions. They look gorgeous and manage to strike the balance between simplicity and complexity. Functions make sense and you manage to Get Things Done.

So what’s not to like?

One small issue. I plan my tasks the night before where I prioritise the majority of my work related and a small number of personal tasks during the day. However, there is no way to schedule tasks for the next evening unless you stay up until after midnight or do this in the morning.

One big issue. I love my iPhone and MacBook. They are my workhorses at home. But, at work, I’m using CentOS with a Windows 10 VM. I understand that an app for other operating systems would be a big ask but I don’t understand why there’s not a web version?

I would love to continue being productive at work without having to use my phone when I have a big screen, keyboard and mouse. I’m aware that I can email new tasks to myself but I’m referring to the ability to view all projects and tasks on my big screen. 

It’s 2019 guys, you can do this!

I don’t normally write reviews, and I certainly don’t normally spend a tenner on an app...but I am so chuffed with Things. 

Yes, you could get results using Apples notes, reminders and calendar. 
But that’s a real flaff compared to this single app. 

Clean, simple and effective. 
In just 20 minutes I started to feel I was getting things (no pun intended) in order and could feel my mind clearing. 

Top marks 👍
author: Mr_Fibbles

title: Where has Things been all my life!?
body:
I don’t write that many reviews so an App has to be quite exceptional for me to spend a bit of time doing so... and Things is exceptional.. and more!

After struggling by with Apple Reminders and other inferior to do lists for years a friend said for me to try this... and I was hooked.

As a busy engineer I run many projects simultaneously and this is the app I now use. Simple to use, powerful and reliable.

I also use it for my to dos around the home so please don’t think it’s all business.

Don’t get me wrong, it’s not cheap and the iPad and Mac versions are quite an extra cost but it’s a small price for perfection.
author: Blackswann1979

title: Truly awesome
body: Easy to use immediately...simple but so effective in GSD. I just went through the full tutorial and it’s even better than I thought. Use this every day now!
author: Leighton girling

title: Apple Watch Magic
body:
For me the real reason I love this app is it’s Apple Watch complication. It does what no other reminders app does and that’s show you a constant reminder throughout the day. Every other app wants you to set a time or date. 
One request would be for the watch complication to change the displayed reminder on each glance at the watch face.
That what you can set a list of stuff you need to do that day but none of them at specific times and every glance at the watch your reminded of a different task.
author: ConorMcg

title: In awe of this app
body:
I am in awe of this application. Paired with Things on all my iOS devices and my Mac (yeah, I'm one of those folk!), Things has really revolutionised my habits. Once upon a time I continuously put off completing tasks, and was crazy forgetful about everything. Now, I simply rely upon Things to remember for me, and to prod me into doing stuff on time.

It took a while to actually form the habit of listing my to-dos in the app, but once I started, it became almost automatic. Things has also become so beautiful over the years, especially the new Dark Mode. The design and intuition that’s gone into it is stunning. I love it, and recommend it to everyone. One thing I would really like to draw attention to is the sync speed between devices — it is SO fast. I honestly don’t know how they manage it. 

It's only now that I'm writing a review (something I never do!), but as a result I can vouch that Things is one of the best apps I've used over a multi-year period. To think that the team are still adding small quality of life features every now and then! I think it’s perfect already, but you can be sure they’ll think of something.
author: JTG~G

title: Perfect for me
body: Everything I need is here and the design is refined enough to not get over complicated even with some very powerful tools
author: Trump Egg ltd

title: Wish the icon was better
body: Beautiful design inside, but sadly the app icon itself is quite ugly when sitting next to other apps. Needs to be more minimalist and clean.
author: JLKingsley

title: Good but not as user friendly as you’d expect
body: This is a handy app especially as it can link to Apple Watch and you can add reminders that way. However, it’s not always easy to navigate. How do you delete a recurring item permanently? All it seems to do it delete it for that week. After trying seemingly every option I can access I still can’t find it, meaning I can’t permanently delete a reminder for a task which I no longer need to do, reducing the usefulness of the app. It needs to be easier to do simple things.

title: The best for organising your life
body:
I love Things3 and have been using it on all of my devices. It is highly customisable has a very elegant design. 

Feature request:

I’d love a view called ‘This Week’ which looks like a calendar view and shows you all your tasks for the week. For me, this would make the app the ultimate tool for organising. I have ADHD and right now I also need to look at a calendar to visualise my time.

Better features for visualisation would be amazing.
author: Rozzoll

title: Worth the money

I balked at Things 3 due to the price, but after being frustrated by the other options I decided to give it a go. I admit, the team at Cultured Code have created the perfect app which is worth the money. You certainly get what you pay for. Well done, everyone.

body:
Not the best todo app out there and it’s way overpriced,

I was hoping it could interact with the iOS reminders app but it will only import the items and then deletes them from the reminder app after they are imported.

I’m also disappointed that you have to pay another £19.99 if you want to use this basic app on your iPad.

author: 9595Luke

title: Well thought out, but (still) not perfect yet
body:
(Note, I never used earlier generations of things so I'm coming to this version fresh)

I like the design - you've clearly put a lot of thought and work into meeting people's needs while also keeping it simple. It shows, and deserves to be highlighted.

I've found a couple of niggles though:

1. The use of space is a bit too lavish in some places.
Overall, I like what you've done in giving each task enough space to separate it from its neighbours, but a checklist is a single thing, and I think the items should be displayed closer together to express that unity.

2. It could do with templates that aren't repeating tasks / projects.
I have checklists for when I'm going on trips, etc. I want a way to create a project and popular it with the relevant item. For now I've created a "Templates" Area and put things there that I can duplicate then move to where I want them. Trouble is, these things then show up under Anytime.

author: bval19

title: This is a great app but not quite perfect
body:
Firstly, I recommend this app. If you’re using it for yourself as an individual or self employed professional on your own it’s fab. I have it for both iPhone and iPad and it’s great (I don’t have a Mac). 

So I did have three things but the excellent customer support told me how to use the slightly hidden intelligent language parsing in the date picker. So two of three minor issues solved. Great first class customer support too. 
So that leaves the most annoying issue for me, which is task order in the today list, or the upcoming list for that matter. There should be the choice to order these by time of reminder as well as date (in the upcoming list’s case it does group tasks by due day but not reminder time). It especially annoys me on the today list. Just an option in settings to turn on sorting by reminder time would be perfect for me. Personally I’d like to have no due time tasks first in today then tasks with a due time below in order of due time getting later towards the bottom of the list. Having to keep manually reordering things each day is a little tiresome. It’s good that I’m reviewing all the tasks each morning but still, some automation for list order would be super useful and would personally save me that extra little bit of time. 

But other than this grumble I love the app. Fav task management app that I use daily for personal and work tasks. The Apple Watch app integration is great too.

title: Excellent with Apple Watch

author: T D 2

title: Best of the Bunch and improving
body:
I have tried a lot of task managers but Things 3 is my ‘go to’ app, particularly when combined with Bear for notes etc. 

Tags and data manipulation is excellent with huge flexibility to meet your needs as you require and not forced down a particular way of working. I use David Allen’s GTD to great effect with Things 3 - a huge leap forward over previous iterations. 

Developer is responsive and whilst there is an up front cost, this is significantly less that the subscription fees I am paying with other similar apps. 

Keep up the good work.
author: Ducati Multistrada Dave

title: The one, the only, the mighty Things.
body:
Been using Things on and off since v1.

It’s the best of the best but if you want to have the suite across an iPhone, iPad and Mac get ready to spend a pretty penny.

That said it’s still much, much better than paying through the nose every month for the rest of eternity.

The screenshots may give the illusion of something pretty basic but it’s a powerhouse.
author: Dipped In Tea

title: How can GTD be this fun?
body: Things is a marvel. It makes life management a breeze and more than that, a joy! I couldn’t imagine how v2 could be improved but v3 is just extraordinary. The boring side of lists and projects move to the background and the gorgeous UI and completely intuitive workflows make Things unprecedented in its field. Sure it’s not cheap, thank goodness for that as one gets what one pays for. Keep up the work that sets you apart. Thanks for making a suite of one app, that doesn’t have me resenting getting things done!
author: mac98aop

title: It's great, but no non-mac support
body:
I bought this app as I was in search of a great to-do list and this has great reviews. It was, hand on heart, the most expensive app I've ever bought but I felt it would be worth it. I can confirm it's a well designed app that is quite easy to use, 

HOWEVER,

1. They only support Apple devices. So if you only have an iPhone but otherwise use PCs you have no other way of accessing your list. Not even a web interface. This is a giant pain not only for easy accessibility but also it's often easier to see things on a bigger screen to see the bigger picture, move things around, plan, etc. I'd rather use my phone for quick entry and my PC to categorise, plan, set deadlines, etc.

2. I can't find a way to pull up a list of ALL my outstanding items. Maybe not something most people would want but I find it useful. 

So for me it's just not the app I need. I hope someone else finds this info useful before they drop a fiver on an app with limited portability.

title: Good

author: Longphi

title: Great app; use it every day
body:
Things simply keeps my life organised. I love the Integration with Apple's Reminders and Calendars. Through Siri I can easily input new tasks on the fly. 

The today view (opened quickly with Siri shortcuts) nicely shows all things to be done today underneath a list of Calendars events. 

The Apple watch app is great at the supermarket where the shopping list can be displayed and checked off. I've got headings setup based on the supermarket's aisles so the items needed are in the correct order. 

There's not a lot I would change. A nice addition would be a quick link to today's events in the Calendar app with a tap on the events list in Things' today view, if this is technically possible. 

Throughout recommended!

title: Brilliant to-do app
body:
I’ve used a range of to-do apps over the years eventually settling on one that worked well across platforms and was free (and supported moveable sub tasks). However, Things is functionally richer with a more enjoyable interface. It does what I need for simple tasks as well as for more complex situations. 

In particular I like being able to slide up the blue + symbol and add a task to where I want (eg on a particular day in the upcoming calendar view, or to a particular project (sliding up the + in the anytime view). 

Also handy is being able to do a voice input to add a task to Things using my Apple Watch.

author: PhilipPanis87

title: Really is very good
body:
Ok, so you’ve read the reviews but still not sure if you should pay a full tenner for Things3... maybe try some of the free ones again...
Well, although MinimaList and Microsoft ToDo are good alternatives to the retiring Wunderlist, Things3 really is excellent. It’s certainly everything I need. 
Has all the functions you need without being complicated. It’s intuitive in use, has a classy clean style, and there are no ads at all. 
Importantly, you can set priorities, tags, dates and reminders - so you really can use it to schedule and prioritise your tasks across a week or month.
If you need more than a simple checklist, but don’t want to have to spend ages learning how to use a complicated app - you can do worse than Things3. 
One of the best tenners I’ve spent in a long time.

author: immelda marcos

title: Invasion of privacy
body: I downloaded then immediately deleted Things 3. As soon as I opened it I went to open a free Things Cloud account so I could use cloud sync across my devices. I thought it was strange they didn’t offer sync via iCloud and thought I’d scan through the T&Cs. I’m glad I did. Cultured Code require you to give them complete access to your todo list which they can do anything they like with. Reproduce, modify, create derivative works, communicate and distribute. I think it’s disgusting they hide this in the small print. And their privacy policy, weirdly, completely overlooks the license you grant them to distribute what could be extremely confidential data. It makes no mention of it anywhere. Pretty sure this isn’t GDPR compliant and I really hope the new EU laws bite this company on the bum. Isn’t it enough that we pay £10 for the app? You want your greedy paws on our data as well. What a deceitful company.

author: p0lip0li

title: Ideal Task Manager
body:
Things is an incredibly powerful and flexible way to manage to do lists and simple projects across multiple devices. I like the ability to tag or create collections and the search function is really powerful. 

The interface is intuitive and can be configured in different ways to suit how you want to use it - so it works for you rather than the other way round. You need to get into good habits like capturing actions (which is made easier by the links with other apps) and regularly reviewing and updating status. 

Not the cheapest, but having used other task managers I would say this is by far the best. It was money well spent when I consider the time it’s saved me by being more organised and efficient- it’s probably paid for itself, in terms of time saved, every month.

author: fatgeet

title: £30 well spent...
body:
I hate lists, I hate to-dos, I hate reminders.... I love Things 3.

I've spent my entire life doing things because they need doing; if I really need to remember something I'll put it in a calendar. However the number of things I need to track was getting crazy.

I heard numerous podcasts saying how nice Things was so I tried on the iPhone  version and immediately loved it.

It has an easy, flexible interface which meant I could put tasks when i thought I'd do them, like a calendar.
 I can put personal stuff that occurs to me at work to do this evening.
I can add bulleted thoughts to a task and change the order.
I can group tasks into a project.
I can move things around so easily to help me work out what to do next.
The Watch app is awesome- I was walking along suddenly thought of something to do tapped the complication recorded what I needed to do (Watch Series 1) and it appeared on my iPhone waiting to be triaged.

I can give the email address to my partner so she can email me things to do. Which don't appear in my Today list, but are on the queue to be thought about.

title: Best UI but needs a day planning feature!
body:
One of the best and most mature todo apps with a great intuitive UI. Very few other options out there with native Mac/iOS apps and so many features.

The only problem is : the latest research shows that the most successful and productive people don’t use todo apps, they use calendars (google it) ! If doesn’t get scheduled, it won’t happen as reliably. Plus, a calendar keeps you honest and realistic as to how many things you can schedule in a day, which helps avoid the « never ending todo list of doom » problem.

Things allows you to schedule tasks to a day only, and even though it now has a reminder feature, this is not enough : there is no notion of task duration, and no way to simply drag a task to a specific space on your day, so you can instantly visualize it.

There are some other apps based on this concept (Plan, Sorted, TickTick) but they’re nowhere near as feature rich. If Things added that one feature, it would completely eat this market !

title: A mixed bag
body:
I'm happy to support app developers by buying apps. However, having spent nearly £60 upgrading to Things 3 on my Mac and iPhone, I think it's disingenuous to tell me that Things 2 on my iPad will no longer sync within Things Cloud, unless I spend another £20 on upgrading the iPad app. Presumably the wire format hasn't changed, so there's no technical reason for this limitation.

Things 3 has a sweet new UI and interaction model, but it's not necessarily more efficient. For example, you can no longer reschedule a to-do directly from the Today view in the iOS app; you have to move it to your Inbox first. EDIT: It turns out you can do this by swiping the to-do right, but it's not very discoverable.

The Logbook view needs some serious performance optimisation because scrolling through the thousands of to-dos I've accumulated during eight years is much slower than it was in Things 2. Finally, add in that the developers have ignored a simple question I have asked (twice) on Twitter and the financial investment begins to sting a bit.

title: Devil's advocate
body:
The new Things is clearly a powerful and sleek beast . I haven't though seen many reviews of Things iOS that mention downsides . I do wonder how anyone can assess a new app thoroughly enough to confidently award 5 stars, within days of its release . To perhaps redress the balance (or is it an 'outpouring of negativity'), here are my rough jottings of aspects of Things 3 that I find a turn off:
Loss of functionality from Things 2 as listed in the Things Support article e.g. Projects list gone, can no longer set an advance warning of a deadline, can no longer filter by 'no tag', nor by deadline, cannot change font size, no time stamp inside to-dos. Plus:
No alphabetical sort of projects in sidebar
No collapsing of areas in "sidebar "
Spotlight integration is gone.
Additionally:
No collapsing of the new headings within projects 
Loss of shading impedes ease of the "form filling " aspect of using the app. Things 2 had a superb UI design, attractive and guiding  the user 's eye. We now have white space 
Loss of colour coding of areas - no green icons, except in Someday 
No location-based to dos 
Still no repeating to dos in projects 
Too much white space on the screen ( see above). It's harsh on the eye and creates glare.
Things 3 "What's new" says " When you open a to-do, it smoothly transforms into a clear white piece of paper, ready for your thoughts. " A blank canvas may be helpful if I'm writing a book or a journal, but Things is essentially a database and I find the structure of a form helpful when entering data.
Notes still cannot be hidden
No undo or cancel button e.g. Creating a new to do
I have difficulty in moving around the app - I'm not finding it intuitive 
You can't switch to landscape view  (being locked in portrait feels claustrophobic to me)
The new 'headings' feature looks quite useful, but what is its intended purpose? If it's really defining a sub-task, why can't you mark it 'done'?
The checklist feature is rather in the same category. Nifty, but isn't it really a sub-task? I can't figure out how to archive a checklist for future use, a feature that would be very handy and would justify the use of the term 'checklist'.
The very useful improvements and new features of Things 3 have probably all been covered in the avalanche of positive reviews, so I won't mention them here. It is a good app in many ways , but a long way (in my view) from being brilliant . It is a surprise to me that I much prefer Things 2! Having said that, my 2 star marking is tongue-in-cheek - or just plain cheek! - the app is much better than that. But when you're the devil's advocate, needs must😊. I hope the developer will enhance and improve the features of Things 3, to build on the excellent work they have already done.

4. Freely rename Upcoming, Anytime, and Someday.

title: Polished, practical and nearly perfect
body:
I'd always struggled a bit with Things 2; while I liked the idea the workflow seemed a bit clunky  times and never really clicked (too much tapping at fields and menus). As a result I ended up abandoning it after a few months. 

Things 3 changes all that; the interface is really polished and fluid and you can create new todos and move them around really easily. The redesigned interface lays out information clearly, and animations which both make the app a pleasure to use and highlight important information.  It's pretty much the most polished app I've used - every pixel and animation has clearly been obsessed over.

No app is perfect, though and there are a couple of things that I'd like to see, particularly:

- A fully featured extension (at the moment it just adds the todo to the inbox which is fine but I'd like to select where they go).
- Repeating to dos in projects: at the moment they exist in areas. I heard that this would be changed in a future update. 
- And finally the natural language entry box is a bit hidden. Had to read the manual to find it (pull down on the date selector to get  the entry box). 

To do apps are a personal thing; what works well for me might be to rigid or too unstructured for someone else. Things is flexible enough to be used as a strict GTD app or more causally as a general list of things to do.  I've tried pretty much every major to do app, from Omnifocus to ToDoist and after a month or so of use (I was in the beta for a bit) Things is the one I'm going to stick with.

title: Calendar Integration
body:
Things is an outstanding task manager with exceptional design and a highly intuitive structure built around Areas and Projects. It strikes a rare balance between simplicity and depth, making task capture, planning, and review both efficient and enjoyable.

The one notable limitation is the lack of calendar visibility for time-based tasks. Scheduled tasks do not appear in external calendars like Fantastical, Apple Calendar, or Google Calendar, which creates friction for users who rely on time-blocking.

With native calendar integration for scheduled tasks, Things would evolve from an excellent task manager into a complete planning system. Even as it stands, it remains one of the most thoughtfully designed productivity apps available.

title: The Epitome of Simplicity and Productivity
body:
When it comes to organizing my life and staying on top of my tasks, Things 3 has truly been a game-changer. This meticulously designed app has managed to strike the perfect balance between simplicity and functionality, making it an indispensable tool for boosting productivity.

From the moment you open Things 3, its clean and intuitive interface welcomes you with open arms. Creating tasks, setting due dates, and organizing projects have never been easier or more enjoyable. The app’s smooth navigation and seamless integration across all my devices ensure that I never miss a beat, whether I’m on my phone, tablet, or computer.

What truly sets Things 3 apart is its attention to detail. The app understands the importance of focus and provides a clutter-free environment, allowing me to concentrate solely on my tasks. Its powerful features, such as tags, deadlines, and checklists, offer a sense of control and help me prioritize effectively.

Furthermore, Things 3 goes beyond mere task management by incorporating a Today view, which intelligently presents me with the tasks I need to tackle each day. The app’s robust reminder system ensures that deadlines are never missed, keeping me on track and reducing stress.

In summary, Things 3 has revolutionized the way I approach my to-do list. Its minimalist design, seamless synchronization, and thoughtful features have transformed the tedious process of task management into a delightful experience. Whether you’re a busy professional or a meticulous planner, Things 3 is the ultimate companion for taking control of your life.

title: One of the best app ever used.
body:
I just love this application to keep track of the things I have to do at work and home. I have purchased both the iPhone and the Mac App separately and it’s totally worth the money I paid. Though on the expensive side - if you think long term, it kinda works out. 

1. In love with the UI and animations. 
2. The keyboard shortcuts are well thought off. It’s almost like an in-build Apple designed app. 
3. Sync works perfectly well. 
4. Today view with the projects categorically shown. 
5. Scheduling works like a charm, natural language inside the “when” view is very well thought off. You can type 15feb 11 and it will start showing recommendations. 
6. Task repeat feature is also amazing, with both the recurring and the recurring on completion. 
7. Reminders with notifications across all devices. 
8. Integration with Calendars shows all the important events in Today and Upcoming views. 
9. Email to things where you can email your task from your inbox of your choice. 
10. Drag-Drop and multiple window support is very useful for planning your day. 

I think I can go on, but let me end it here so that it doesn’t look like their feature list :P

Kudos to the team at Cultured Code. I am a huge fan now.

title: Amazing app.
body:
This is a really beautiful piece of software with a few things missing. 

Quick take: TAGS needs major improvements on iOS and iPadOS. Take cues from MacOS please. 

First the good. I am someone who doesn’t stray from the stock iOS apps easily. I will use notes, reminders, calendar, etc by Apple only, since it’s simple and does what I need. But wow, this app is something truly amazing. From the moment you use it the first time, it’s evident that the developers were really passionate about this project and the passion reflect clearly onto the UI of the app. The stock reminders app got a major refresh in iOS 13 and I thought I’d be only using that. But this app is just beyond amazing on the functionality it provides that just can’t be matched with the stock reminders app.   

Obviously, nothing is perfect. There’s always room for improvement. 

Key things needed to further refine this already amazing app: 

1. Allow us to ‘manage’ tags directly. Right now the only way I’ve found to manage/edit tags is to select a current task, and then select the tags menu from it and THEN we are given the option to edit tags. This option should not be hidden under so many lays and should be more easily viewable. Also, the way tags appear at the top of to-do’s on Mac, is really handy. A similar feature on phone and iPad would be nice. 

2. Allow the user to customise the app icon. Quite a few apps have adopted the ‘customisable’ app option allowing the user to choose from various colour pallets. Makes the user like the app more and (at least in my case) I tend to keep it on my home screen rather than hidden in a folder, thus increasing my usage. 

3. (More of a request) Please allow us to rename the “Inbox” tab. Inbox just doesn’t feel right. “To-do” “Reminders” etc etc, if only users had the choice. 🤔

title: Non posso farne a meno
body:
Uso questa app almeno dal 2015 (se non prima, ormai non ricordo più…), ed è quell’app che, se mi dicessero “Puoi tenere una sola app sul tuo iPhone, quale scegli?”, sarebbe senza esitazione questa. Mi permette di svuotare la mia testa da tutti i milioni di To-Do che mi vengono in mente, urgenti e non, importanti e non, e mi permette di organizzarli con un senso senza perdermene neanche uno. È facilissimo rivederli, spostarli, trasformarli; con questa app ho imparato (e continuo ad imparare — perché ogni tanto mi perdo, ma per com’è fatta basta poco per rientrare in carreggiata) ad essere efficiente nella gestione della mia vita. 

 Apprezzo moltissimo anche il pagamento unico: il prezzo è sì elevato, ma secondo me vale tutti i soldi che costa, e personalmente preferisco di gran lunga pagare un alto costo iniziale ed usare l’app per anni (appunto, la uso da più di 8 anni…), piuttosto che pagare mille abbonamenti che ti succhiano soldi costantemente. 

 Come nuove caratteristiche mi piacerebbe in futuro vedere le seguenti: 
- possibilità di segnare un To-Do come “Iniziato” (e non spuntarlo per forza come finito): a volte ci sono To-Do lunghi, che non sono progetti o non hanno diversi step, ma sarebbe carino poter segnare di averli iniziati; 
- localizzazione dei To-Do; 
- condivisione di To-Do, progetti o intere aree con altri utenti. 
Allora l’app sarà veramente PERFETTA.

title: Buona ma... da MIGLIORARE!
body:
Grafica Minimal, completa per l’utilizzo base ma con alcune funzionalità sicuramente da implementare o perfezionare.
Alcuni spunti da verificare:

*La possibilità di inserire una nuova attività direttamente ad "Oggi", cliccando sul pulsante +, senza dover necessariamente salvarle in "Entrata" per poi doverla spostare in un secondo momento.
 
*Le attività con scadenza definita dovrebbero essere raggruppate per ordine temporale, senza trovare attività poste alla fine dell'elenco solo perché inserite per ultime.
 
*La possibilità di assegnare un grado di Priorità alle varie attività nel momento in cui vengono schedulate.
 
*La possibilità di pianificare un’attività con ulteriori target come "Domani, alla fine della settimana, Prossima settimana... etc…" invece è possibile solamente pianificare ad "Oggi, questa sera e Prima o poi".
 
*L'inserimento di una notifica che al mattino (ad orari stabiliti dall'utente) effettui un riassunto delle attività schedulate in giornata ed una a fine serata fornisca un resoconto di quelle svolte.
 
*La possibilità di modificare le azioni di scorrimento sulle attività schedulate (swipe dx o sx), per decidere che azione eseguire (Pianifica, Elimina, completa... etc).
 
*La possibilità di condividere attività con altri utenti (esempio Componenti del nucleo familiare).
 
*L'abilitazione dell'autenticazione a due fattori tramite App per l'accesso, lo sblocco solamente tramite PIN o Face-ID
 
In conclusione, quando verranno implementate ulteriori features per renderla molto più versatile (magari qualcuna tra quelle elencate) sicuramente darò 5 stelle, rapporto qualità prezzo rimane comunque competitiva con altre app di questo genere 👍🏻

title: Da sviluppare
body:
L’ho utilizzata un po’ e restituita. È fatta bene ma non per me, anche se ho cercato il più possibile di adattarmi. Il primo inconveniente è che non si possono inserire o modificare appuntamenti sul calendario, ma solo leggerli. 
Nel riepilogo dei progetti “Prossimamente” non è possibile ordinarli e soprattutto non ci sono le priorità, ma solo i tag, diventando un po’ tortuoso l’inserimento. 
Mi sarebbe piaciuto avere direttamente l’elenco dei tag, e non cercarli ogni volta. Condivido l’aspetto minimal ma deve avere qualche opzione di più per renderla più versatile.

title: Time management “zen”
body:
A livello professionale esistono solo due app ai vertici: Omnifocus e Things. Il primo è molto più completo e migliore (forse) per determinate attività molto complesse, anche se le distanza si stanno assottigliando molto. Things invece riesce ad essere di utilizzo estremamente semplice ma completo allo stesso tempo! 

Utilizzo questa App da svariati anni. L’ho tradita con Omnifocus solo per un paio di volte perché Things è molto lenta negli aggiornamenti. Ma quando gli sviluppatori fanno qualcosa, la fanno sempre bene. Un po’ in stile Apple. 

Questa App è per me semplicemente la numero uno al mondo, senza se e senza ma! Per poterla sfruttare al meglio è opportuno conoscere i principi del GTD. Un ottimo passo è acquistare su Amazon l’ebook “padrone del tempo”. 

La consiglio a chiunque voglia prendere il controllo della propria vita.

Trovo però una mancanza fondamentale nella app per Apple Watch: è infatti possibile vedere sull’appellativo Watch i soli task della giornata odierna e non quelli immediatamente futuri o di progetti specifici. Spero davvero che gli sviluppatori implementeranno questa a possibilità su Apple Watch altrimenti così come è ha una grossa mancanza a mio avviso. Se così sarà vedrò di aumentare la valutazione, per il momento 3 stelle! Buon lavoro

title: I don’t understand the hype
body:
This app is stable and easy to use but in my personal opinion, there’s too much hype surrounding it. 
A few annoying issues: 1) it doesn’t allow to attach anything to notes. Any other task manager allows to do this. 
2) it has no natural language recognition. 
3) the app has limited calendar options/integrations and uses proprietary formats for reminders. If you use popular calendars such as Fantastical 2, you will not be able to link the two apps because the calendar apps will only be able to read reminders in the native iOS app but Things does not sync with the native reminders app. In essence, reminders created within Things will only be accessible within Things. Very annoying, considering other reminder apps don’t have this shortcoming. 
4) for reminders with a longer title, only the first words are displayed, followed by “...”. It would be much better to see the entire title in 2 lines, so that everything is visible at a single glance. 

All in all, I bought this app following the hype around it. After many months using it, I am still frustrated by the numerous limitations and surprised by its popularity (good graphics and quick swipes are in my opinion insufficient)
author: GMG18

title: Ne ho provate tante ma questa è la migliore
body:
Secondo me è la migliore app per la produttività personale. Prima ho studiato il metodo GTD e poi ho cercato di applicare i concetti utilizzando diverse app per testarle e vedere la più pratica da adottare. 
Non ha tutte le funzionalità che occorrono per applicare alla lettera il metodo GTD ma dopo un po’ che la usi ti rendi conto che è meglio così. Chi ha letto il libro sa che l’autore predilige la carta, quindi il sistema che propone è configurato per una soluzione mista (carta + digitale). Però se tu (come me) preferisci una soluzione completamente digitale, devi adattare i concetti e snellire il sistema. Con questa app sei praticamente guidato (oserei dire “obbligato”) a creare un buon sistema GTD Personale. 
Non mi metto a descrivere tutte le caratteristiche (alcune veramente geniali) dell’app perché sono tantissime. 
Unico neo: per lavorare bene devi avere anche la versione per Mac e dovrai comperarla a parte. La spesa complessiva sembra alta a prima vista, ma ti assicuro che il sistema se è ben applicato ti cambia la vita. 
Tieni conto che il pagamento li fai una volta e basta, mentre per alcune soluzioni concorrenti, se vuoi le stesse funzionalità, devi sottoscrivere un abbonamento da pagare periodicamente.

title: Diverse mancanze
body:
Uso Things quotidianamente da un anno. Inizio subito col dire che il prezzo non è alto se si considera che si paga una tantum.

Things è in grado di coniugare svago e lavoro, uso blando e uso intenso, imponendoti il suo metodo che funziona ed è efficace. Tutto questo è reso possibile dall’interfaccia. L’unica app con un’interfaccia fatta bene, davvero.

All’inizio è stato amore a prima vista poi piano piano sono venute fuori alcune mancanze che non mi permettono di usarlo come vorrei:

ALLEGATI
Non ci sono. Troppe volte un’attività è correlata ad uno o più file e averli allegati non è solo una comodità ma anche una necessità.

PROMEMORIA BASATI SULLA POSIZIONE
Non sono indispensabili però, come per gli allegati, è una funzionalità che anche le app gratuite hanno.

PROGETTI
I progetti sono fantastici. Non ho trovato niente di simile su altre app. Però avete fatto 30, potevate far 31: le note all’interno dei progetti possono essere posizionate solo sotto il titolo. Io vorrei poter metterle ovunque.

APPLE WATCH
L’app per Apple Watch è troppo minimale: si possono solo vedere le attività di Oggi e aggiungere attività solo su Oggi o Entrata.

title: L’app con cui organizzo la mia vita
body:
Le app che gestiscono i to-do sono estremamente soggettive. Ogni app ha il suo approccio e ognuno giustamente preferirà un’app diversa. Per me, Things è fenomenale. Mi permette di inserire le mie attività, cose che voglio fare o che devo fare, e dimenticarmene. Mi libera la mente fino al giorno appropriato, quando quelle attività salteranno di nuovo fuori.

Un’altra cosa fenomenale è la velocità con cui posso inserire una attività nella “Inbox”. Ovunque sono, mi ricordo di qualcosa - trak - la inserisco in Things. Poi a casa o quando ho tempo la categorizzerò con tag, area, progetto, data e scadenza.

La combinazione delle 3 app per le 3 piattaforme non è economica. Ma se vi trovate bene, sarete felici di averle acquistate.

Una cosa manca: la collaborazione, condividere facilmente un progetto con qualcuno e lavorarci insieme, con la stessa immediatezza con cui faccio ogni altra cosa su Things. Ma gli sviluppatori sono estremamente attivi e il servizio cloud è super affidabile. 5 stelle.

title: Integrata con Airmail o Spark è una bomba
body:
La uso tantissimo per lavoro e devo dire che l’interfaccia e la facilità di utilizzo mi aiutano a non perdere task da fare.

La funzionalità che mi ha convinto ad acquistarla è la schermata con i todo + integrazione con calendario.
Avere in una unica schermata un recap di appuntamenti e to do e fondamentale per organizzare al meglio la giornata.

Consiglio vivamente di utilizzare un client di posta tipo Airmail o Spark per sfruttare le integrazioni tra la mail e il todo.

In un click potete categorizzare la mail nella lista di to do in base al progetto e recuperare in un secondo momento la mail a cui rispondere. Infatti crea automaticamente un task con l’oggetto della mail come titolo e nella descrizione genera un link che aprirà il programma di posta e alla mail specifica a cui rispondere.

Ha alcune pecche se confrontata con altre app simili (es. notifiche su scadenze promemoria o mancanza upoad di file su singolo task) però il segreto probabilmente sta proprio nella semplicità dell’interfaccia e nella metodologia che ti obbliga a trovare e tenere.

La cosa poco che non apprezzo è il dover pagare separatamente per ogni dispositivo (mobile - tablet - computer).

Consiglierei, inoltre, agli sviluppatori, di inserire la possibilità di far scattare l'alert con il promemoria anche nei giorni precedenti la data dell'impegno fissato.
Quest'ultimo è il motivo per cui do 4 stelle anziché 5.
author: Super40

title: Almost perfect!
body:
I love this app, it’s absolutely beautiful and helpful! I use it everyday for my private life and work! I just think there are some small things missing...
Please guys why you don’t add the possibility to flag the activities that don’t have a due date but I need to keep highlighted. Please add the possibility to have a deadline longer than 14 days! Please give us the possibility to create smart list filtered by tags or due date!!
With this small improvements this app could be PERFECT, unless I have to switch to another one... 😔
author: Riccardo Sforza

title: Da migliorare complicazione Apple Watch
body:
L’applicazione non è male molto intuitiva e molto bella graficamente. Per quanto mi riguarda ha una grossa pecca, purtroppo la complicazione per l’apple Watch non aggiorna gli impegni riportati nell’applicazione dell’iPhone. Sotto questo aspetto è decisamente da migliorare!!!

Aggiornamento
Ho risolto disinstallando l’applicazione dall’apple watch e reinstallando. Ora va tutto bene!!! A questo punto posso tranquillamente dire che è davvero un ottima applicazione!!!
author: Arckdan

title: Ottima applicazione
body:
Come da titolo. Uso l’applicazione oramai da un anno e mi sono trovato vernante bene fin dal primo momento. La uso principalmente per organizzare al meglio il mio lavoro per la programmazione degli interventi, creare progetti e segnarmi le attività da svolgere dai clienti. 
Sarebbe comodo avere integrato un calendario direttamente nell’applicazione così da evitare di dover passare da Things a calendario. 
Per il resto è proprio ottima.
Complimenti agli sviluppatori.
author: Baobabpuzzi

title: Perfetta, ma in continuo aggiornamento
body: Un app eccellente per ricordarsi le cose
author: Giocatore73

title: Bene Ma..
body:
Grande applicazione ma manca l’integrazione con Windows e dato che nei posti di lavoro si usa solo quest’ultimo non posso usarla in tutti i device. 

Resto in attesa di rilascio per nuove piattaforme VE LO CHIEDO DA ANNI ORMAI
author: sonda423

title: NON APPRE SU APPLE WATCH
body: ho provato in tutti i modi ma NON APPARE SU APPLE WATCH. COMPLETAMENTE INUTILE. UNA RAPINA
author: MikUlisse

title: Things 3
body:
È il GTD perfetto per le mie esigenze: minimale, completo, funzionale e preciso.

È il GTD perfetto per me: non è complesso e troppo ricco per le mie necessita come lo sarebbe OmniFocus ma più modulare e completo dei promemoria di default di iOS.

Accompagna la mia quotidianità e mi permette di tenere sotto controllo i task più semplici come la spesa a cosa più impegnativi come progetti lavorativi.

Estremamente consigliato, applicazione fantastica.
author: suzughia

title: Lo adoro! c’è molto da dire
body:
Da un anno sto dietro questa applicazione ma ero indecisa visto avevo già acquistato la versione precedente anni prima. Finalmente da qualche settimana ho comprato Things 3 e da appena fatto il tutorial iniziale ho apprezzato l’intuitività e potenzialità e facilità d’uso. Interfaccia da 5 stelle ben curata e aggiornata. 
Ormai la uso facilmente per tenere traccia di tutti gli impegni a breve, più futuri o astratti prima o poi e l’App decide dove categorizzarla senza che dobbiamo pensarci. Vengono categorizzate a seconda se hanno una scadenza o un Tag. La uso davvero per segnarmi, ricordarmi e annotare tutti i della giornata, delle note e i promemoria. È un’ App intelligentissima e perspicace che interagisce con le principali App di sistema cosi che ovunque abbiamo segnato delle cose non le perderemo ne dovremo segnarle in più posti due volte. La nuova versione è quindi incredibile, promossa indubbiamente e senz’altro vale la pena passare dalla 2 alla 3 e con questa recensione ho inteso sottoscriverlo. 
Grazie agli sviluppatori
author: appmartini

title: Complimenti, ci siete riusciti!
body:
Da sviluppatore iOS che sono, mi permetto di dire che quest’app racchiude quello che secondo me deve avere ciascuna app: semplicità nell’idea e massima intuitività per raggiungere l’obiettivo a cui mira. Mai provato un’esperienza utente così efficace, e nemmeno un app così bella da usare! Ho acquistato anche quella per Mac, dopo il periodo di prova. È diventato uno strumento quotidiano per me, sia per vita privata che lavorativa.

I miei più sinceri complimenti a questo fantastico team!
author: Bellots

title: Più promemoria
body: Aggiungete la possibilità di mettere almeno 3 promemoria anche giorni prima o personalizzati e sarebbe l’ideale in tutti i casi!!!
author: Piero8728

title: Veramente soddisfatto
body: Ho sempre cercato un’app che mi permettesse di organizzare in maniera precisa e dettagliata gli impegni lavorativi e personali; things 3 rispetta appieno le caratteristiche sopra elencate. Ritengo sia la migliore app al giorno d’oggi.
author: Totò633

title: Beautiful
body: Beautiful Design. Smooth UX. Well done.
author: I’ll tell you

title: Non cambiatela
body:
Ormai io (come gli altri utenti) ho inserito questa app nella mia routine quotidiana....
Perfezionarla è bene ma non stravolgetela!!!!
