title: THE BEST
body: The best productivity app ever tried!! It’s amazing and you can manage a lot of different tasks!
author: pietro_pelizzari

title: Esagerati!
body: È come va “promemoria” di Apple, ma con meno funzioni. Ad esempio “ricordamelo in un posto” o in Apple Watch, dove non posso consultare gli impegni dei giorni successivi (cosa che posso fare sul’app nativa di Apple) ma solo gli impegni di oggi...a proposito di “impegni”, impegnatevi! Per 11€ dovrebbe sbalordire, non essere un app carina. Graficamente bella, questo sì.
author: Diego Marcellan

title: Bello ma non perfetto
body:
Anche se uso Things da mesi e mi trovo benissimo, l’app non mi da delle funzioni di promemoria precise (anzi sono lente e macchinose, non intuitive).
Per quanto riguarda la gestione delle cose da fare e sulle scadenze è la migliore dello Store! 5 stelle quando migliorerete la parte promemoria! Grandi
author: Emanuele-review

title: Bella Elegante Intuitiva Utile
body:
Dai tempi lontani di Todo in poi ho usato e provato molte applicazioni.
Things 3 è certamente la più bella, elegante, la più intuitiva e quindi semplice da usare, utile.
Più la uso, più mi diventa indispensabile. L’organizzazione delle idee è così facilitata da avere davvero effetti concreti e positivi sulla produttività. Il processo di lavoro in Things 3 segue e asseconda il flusso naturale delle idee, e l’eleganza del layout gioca un ruolo importante in questo senso.

Qualche limitazione, secondo me, sta invece nella mancata integrazione con iCloud, nell’assenza di un conteggio delle attività nelle varie categorie oltre a quella di Entrata, nella non possibilità assegnare un promemoria anche agli elementi nelle liste di controllo, nella mancanza di un servizio di geolocalizzazione per le attività che si svolgono in luoghi precisi.
È per questi motivi che non ho dato 5 stelle
author: TexMex67

title: Soldi Buttati
body: Confusionaria e priva di aiuti pratici,ingannato dalle recensioni,ci sono app anche gratuite migliori sotto ogni punto di vista.

Allora perché non fate un aggiornamento permettendo di accedere all’applicazione con il Face ID? E magari la modalità portrait per l’iphone xs max e i modelli plus?
Sarebbe davvero perfetta in questo modo. 
P.S. Vi prego, aggiungete il Face ID!!

body:

Comoda l’integrazione col calendario nel quale ora indico solo gli appuntamenti (anche se mi piacerebbe fosse un po’ più evidente)
La sto usando quotidianamente ed è per me un grande aiuto 
Un suggerimento? Mettere facoltativa una conferma prima di passare sul registro una cosa flaggata.. a me sarebbe utile.

body: Ho provato tante app di questo tipo: ne esistono molte e mi spingo ogni mese a provarne di diverse. Tuttavia torno sempre a usare Things, non ne ho ancora trovata una all’altezza. Complimenti agli sviluppatori, prodotto di qualità eccellente.

Really good for personal use as it’s pretty simple.

title: Bella, ma troppo costosa e caotica
body:
Esteticamente niente da dire, bellissima UI.
Per quanto riguarda l’utilizzo, non ci siamo: troppo caotica, nel momento in cui creerete 3-4 progetti o una decina di attività, non capirete più niente. Tutto questo sarebbe stato “perdonabile”, se non fosse per il fatto che quest’app costa ben 11€. 
Non ha alcun senso, ci sono applicazioni che fanno le stesse identiche cose ad un prezzo ben minore se non gratis.
Purtroppo sono molto deluso, considerando anche quanto ne avevo sentito parlare bene.
author: Darthowski

title: Soldi buttati. Molto deluso!
body:
Indubbiamente l'app è ben fatta e pensata, ma mancano delle funzioni essenziali, che da mesi e mesi sono state richieste:
1. Non è possibile scegliere il tempo di snooze.
2. Se si riceve l'avviso di un evento e per caso questo non viene letto o sentito il suo avviso, non viene emesso nessun suono ripetuto per segnalarlo.
3. Cosa assurda, poi, non è possibile scegliere il suono della notifica.
4. Durante la creazione dell'attività non è possibile scegliere l'intervallo di tempo per la ripetizione: bisogna creare prima l'evento e poi tornare nella lista eventi e impostare la ripetizione. 
5. Non è possibile impostare un'allarme a ore diverse. Ad esempio, se volessi un allarme per lo stesso evento impostato una settimana prima non è possibile farlo.
6. Ci vorrebbe un avviso anche per mail.

L'app è davvero troppo costosa per quello che offre e non parliamo del fatto che per la versione ipad vadano sborsati circa il doppio dei soldi, quando altre app migliori e complete sono disponibili con un solo acquisto.

title: Ottima applicazione, ma...
body: L’applicazione è ottima. Ma per renderla quasi perfetta ai livelli di OmniFocus; serve la compatibilità con IPad, in questo modo si può avere un uso più professionale.

title: Tanta roba
body: Assurda
author: ilportammare

title: Lo stato dell'arte per la gestione delle attività
body:
Ne ho provate tante in questi anni testando qualsiasi app tra quelle considerate nel novero delle migliori per iOS e credo che Il team di Cultured Code abbia realizzato una piccola meraviglia, unendo semplicità e immediatezza d'uso alla ricchezza delle funzioni. Certamente come tutte le app può essere migliorata (funziona solo su piattaforma iOS e OS non esiste una versione Windows oppure Web, no file attachment, no abbreviazioni da tastiera per iPad, no bulk editing per tags ecc...) ma Things 3 è un equilibrio armonioso di funzionalità e design. Vale ogni euro speso anche la versione per OS X. Senza contare che quelli di Cultured Code fino ad ora hanno rilasciato una serie di aggiornamenti, (su tutti il 3.4) che testimoniano il loro costante impegno nel renderla ancora migliore.
Un Must Have!

title: App ottima!
body:
L’applicazione é ottima, veramente ben fatta. Vale i soldi di un agenda, che per quanto obsoleta ha i suoi vantaggi rispetto a molte altre app sul genere, ma non rispetto a Things 3, che permette di fare praticamente tutto in fatto di organizzazione, senza dover rinunciare a un design semplice e non confusionario. 
Unica richiesta agli sviluppatori: Per favore cambiate logo dell’App! 
App che merita :)

title: Non arrivano promemoria!!
body: Non è concepibile spendere 10€ per un applicazione e non arrivano le notifiche dei promemoria!!! È da 1 settimana che dimentico le cose perché questa app non fa il suo dovere!
author: Nn l so

title: Non merita tutti questi riconoscimenti
body:
Ho scaricato quest’applicazione pensando di aver trovato finalmente l’app giusta per gestire le mie attività, ma così non è stato.
Molto scarna di funzionalità, fa quasi le stesse cose che già potete fare con l'applicazione Promemoria, anzi in alcuni casi anche meno.
Le grafica è molto semplice, ma lo è anche troppo e ogni cosa richiede più azioni del necessario. Ad esempio, le categorie sono praticamente inutili perché non è possibile vedere quali o quante attività sono presenti al loro interno dalla pagina principale è bisogna aprire ogni volta ognuna di esse. Ma se invece di un'attività avete aggiunto un progetto all'interno di quella categoria, non so bene per quale motivo esso apparirà nella schermata home: per me questo rende tutto molto confusionario. 
L'applicazione per Apple Watch mostra solo le attività del giorno, quindi se per caso avete completato un'attività che non era segnata per quel giorno dovete per forza prendere il telefono.

In generale credo che sia un'app discreta ma non vale assolutamente il prezzo di 10€  e non è adatta a persona con molti impegni che richiedono maggior ordine.
author: iemaaans

title: Perfetta per organizzarsi la vita!
body:
Sono una studentessa universitaria fuori sede e durante la giornata mi vengono sempre in mente mille cose da fare, come spesa, bucato, finire di sistemare gli appunti, controllare le tasse, annotarmi un libro che voglio leggere o una ricetta che voglio imparare... con questa app intuitiva è davvero facile scriversi tutto, specialmente con le varie categorie e le etichette, io ora la uso come guida per tutte le mie giornate. Utilissime le ulteriori note e gli elenchi di controllo che si possono inserire nei vari elenchi.
Per non parlare di quanto sia comoda per organizzare tutto ciò che riguarda una un viaggio: valigie, biglietti, ecc...
Abbinata anche all’app su Mac è perfetta, ma comunque costa molto... in ogni caso si può fare tutto anche solo con l’app sul cellulare!

title: Non si possono aggiungere documenti in pdf
body: App bellissima, praticamente è come avere un agenda 24 ore su 24 con te, peccato che non si possono aggiungere i documenti in pdf. Quindi per questo do 4 stelle.

title: Un’app fondamentale
body:

L’unico appunto secondo me è che non è possibile importare immagini (magari delle piccole anteprime), avesse la possibilità di importarle sarebbe assolutamente perfetta.
Non che non lo sia eh, è completa, facilissima, bella da vedere, un vero piacere usarla.

body: Purtroppo non mi soddisfa. Direi che alla fine è, PER ME, inutile.

Mancano alcune cose.. tipo la possibilità di ripetere una cosa.. ok?! Tipo alla scadenza ti fa la notifica e poi una volta completata viene ricreato il promemoria ogni tot di giorni o data fissa.. esempio ogni 1. Del mese fai questo... a questo punto 5 stele garantite..

Ps lascio 2 stelle perché questa cosa per me è molto importante.. anzi le scadenze sono importanti in se quindi ricordare (senza aggiungerle manualmente ogni volta) è comodo per un app simile.. considerando il €€€€€€

body: Tutto perfetto, mi piacerebbe che implementassero anche la funzione di reminder in base alla posizione
author: Pietro94IT

title: Completa. Ma non per me
body:
Programma completo ed offre numerose funzioni tra cui scadenze, tags, liste di controllo, e suddivisione in progetti. 
Tuttavia mi trovo a dare 3 stelle a causa di cose che uso molto.

• Nell'importazione dei promemoria dall'applicazione Apple, vengono eliminati, senza chiedere conferma. Non ricordo se mi è stato chiesto all'inizio, ma non c'è possibilità di cambiare questa opzione, o esportare i promemoria di nuovo in Promemoria di Apple.

• Navigando su un browser, e usando il tasto condivisione su Things per condividere il collegamento, questo non mostra correttamente il link e non si può aprire, apre la home del sito, a differenza dell app Promemoria, che crea l'anteprima aggiungendo il titolo della pagina e generando l'icona.

• Non c'è possibilità di accedere ai promemoria su Windows, in quanto non esiste un'app o un web cloud con cui accedere.

• L'app non si integra con Spotlight ( o dovrei chiamarlo Siri) costringendomi ad usare la ricerca integrata all'interno dell'applicazione.
author: Max.local

title: Dò 5 stelle, ma
body: L'app è fatta benissimo. Condivido tutto quello scritto nelle altre recensioni. L'unico bug che ho riscontrato è che quando inserisco un promemoria tramite Siri, il numero del badge sull'icona non si aggiorna pur essendo presente il promemoria nella scheda "entrata". Spero risolviate.
author: Maurizio1964

title: Good App, with some missing features and pricey
body:
The app is very good, works without any visible flaw and is quite useful in managing several tasks at the same time.
More collaborative features, iCloud integration (instead of their proprietary sync), attachments, better reminders (geo-based?) have to be added before giving 5 stars.
Prices, though, are insane. More than 80€ (!!!) for the complete set of apps, without even Windows or web-based versions.

title: Things 3 - Well done!
body:
Sono stato sempre molto scettico su questo genere di applicazioni perché: 1) hai di base Calendario e Promemoria che ti aiutano a non dimenticare le cose; 2) sono sempre complicate da usare o hanno comunque un aspetto disordinato che ti aiutano a far più confusione! 
Poi un giorno, grazie ad un aggiornamento del Mac sono costretto ad aprire Mac AppStore e in evidenza vedo Things 3. Mi ha incuriosito e l'ho scaricato in prova gratuita da apposito link (solo per Mac). La prova dura 15 gg. Ma dopo soli 2-3 giorni l'ho acquistato, e subito dopo l'ho preso anche per iPhone e iPad. Ho anche approfittato dello sconto del 20%. Certamente si può migliorare, mancano alcune opzioni ma sono sicuro che il team di sviluppatori è sempre al lavoro per cercare di migliorarlo. La cosa difficile è farlo senza rendere l'app complicata e piena di inutili opzioni. È inutile descrivere le varie funzioni visto che ci sono recensioni ovunque su internet. Things 3 riesce bene nel suo lavoro: quello di aiutarti a fare ordine nella tua mente e nella tua vita, non solo al lavoro. Ti pare poco? Per me questo vale ben più del prezzo pagato (per le tre versioni si spende in tutto circa €90 una tantum, prezzo pieno senza sconto). Non sono pochi, ma se si pensa che molte app del genere funzionano con abbonamenti annuali di importo elevato, Things 3 è relativamente a buon prezzo. Ed è superiore rispetto ai concorrenti. Acquisto consigliato, fatevi un buon regalo, non è la solita app, dietro quell'aspetto pulito in perfetto stile Apple c'è tanto lavoro. Complimenti agli sviluppatori!

title: Elegante ed efficace
body:
È sufficiente dare un’occhiata alla sua interfaccia per rendersi conto che Things non è un’applicazione come le altre. Chi ci ha lavorato lo ha fatto con amore e il programma sembra quasi vivo!
Il look minimalista non deve ingannare. Sotto quelle poche righe quasi sperdute in una pagina bianca, ci sono tante opzioni: scadenze, compiti ripetitivi, tag. È possibile dividere la propria vita in tante sezioni (lavoro, famiglia, hobby, spesa…) e in ognuna di queste inserire compiti e progetti. Ogni mattina selezionemo dalle liste i compiti da fare; altri ce li proporrà il programma, seguendo dei parametri che noi gli avremo inserito.
Things poi si adatta al livello di chi lo usa. Qualcuno ci inserirà giusto qualche lista; altri useranno le tante opzioni che questi propone.
Cosa chiedere di più? Per me niente! Non voglio un programma con tante opzioni che non userò mai. Né voglio che abbassi il prezzo. Per quello che vale, Things costa anche troppo poco!

title: Mai trovato alternative valide a Things

Le funzionalità sono rimaste intatte o migliorate (bella la programmazione che include i calendari) mentre la grafica, che risentiva dell'età, è stata semplificata con uno stile che a me piace molto. Io sono completamente dipendente da Things e se non mi segno le cose da fare qui (anche a distanza di anni, tipo scadenza carta d'identità) me le dimentico, molto semplice 😄 L'ho aggiornata anche su Mac nonostante il prezzo caruccio, ma quando un'app è davvero essenziale come Things il prezzo non conta più di tanto. La uso da parecchi anni, straconsigliata

title: La App es bastante buena, pero...
body:
Me encanta Things. Fue el primer GTD que probé y me sigue pareciendo de los mejores, pero vaya que cobrar tanto por una actualización y encima borrar Things 2 se me hace bastante bajo. 

Como digo, me encanta la app y moría por probar la nueva versión, pero no aporta nada nuevo ni innovador e incluso carece de funciones gratuitas en otros GTD. 

Muy mal Cultured Code. Si iban a tardar tanto y encima cobrar una actualización menor (si muy bonita y todo pero, y la funcionalidad?) al menos hubieran volteado a ver que ofrecía la competencia y ofrecérnoslo mas bonito 🙄🙄

Una compra obligada para aumentar la productividad.

Felicidades a los desarrolladores por esta increíble App. Vale cada peso invertido.

author: Minimal-junkie

title: Clean and simple but
body:
It is a nice app however if you are debating between this and free alternatives, the free one might be better.

First, the widget only refreshes after the app is opened (so in the morning it does not display your to do’s immediately).

Second, things added to your Things calendar are not added to your apple calendar (they should add a feature to enable this in some way).

Third, if you buy it on the phone, you still have to buy it again for you laptop (55 euros!)

Definitely needs improvement and 55 euros is ridiculous for such a simple app.

title: Very useful
body:
Thank you for this app—it’s really handy.

I have one suggestion: sometimes I have multiple to-dos that belong together, but they don’t necessarily warrant creating a full project yet. It would be great if there were a way to group related to-dos by simply dragging one to-do underneath another, without turning them into a project.

I’d find that feature really useful.

title: Things wins
body: A while ago I wrote here that Apple’s own Reminders app could now do everything Things does. I take that back. After receiving a gracious reply from the developers, I gave Things another try (which was easy enough because Things can import most items from Reminders), and it *does* offer more. One gripe is that it lacks dependencies (tasks remaining hidden in the Today, Upcoming and Someday views until some specified other task had been completed), but Reminders doesn’t have that, either. Maybe in a future version? That would rock. Regardless, this is a five star app as it is.

* task titles get shortened just to save space
* fidgety: manually sorting tasks and moving them to this evening. It doesn't save the preferences.

title: Things 3

body:

title: Knallbra app og oppdatering
body:
Things er en knallbra todo-app og implementering av Getting Things Done-prinsippene (bok, finnes i iBooks Store). Stilren design og gode funksjoner. Gjør det lett å dele inn ting du har å gjøre i ansvarsområder, prosjekter og enkelt-handlinger samt sjekklister, og å velge hva som kan gjøres i dag og hva som kan utsettes. Ingen unødvendige taps eller ulogiske menyer.

Versjon 3 gir i min mening gode forbedringer og enda mer fokusert design. Things mangler fortsatt en god måte å delegere handlinger eller prosjekter til andre og samarbeid/deling. Delegering kan dog løses med bruk av merkelapper/tags ol. Things er altså ment for å håndtere dine tasks, evt. For at du selv skal holde styr på hva du har delegert eller venter på, men er ikke en samarbeidsplattform slik som Wunderlist eller lignende. 

Ville egentlig trukket en stjerne for manglende samarbeidsfunksjoner, men den stilrene og effektive implementeringen av GTD er så god at appen likevel får full pott. Litt dyr app, men liker at de går for engangskjøp og ikke abonnement slik som flere av konkurrentene gjør. Billig på lang sikt mao.

title: Beautiful!
body:
Ok, let me put it simply.  This is a beautiful app.  I have owned earlier versions of Things for iPhone, iPad and Mac and this one for iPhone is stunning.  Things 3 has a beautifully clean user interface, it's easy to understand and figure out how to do things (sorry, no pun intended), it's intuitive and way more useful than earlier versions, with checklists and headings.  

There's good documentation on Cultured Code's web site if you want to know more, but the app is so well designed, as long as you know a little bit about GTD (Getting Things Done),  you'll be productive right away without having to read any manuals. 

I also own OmniFocus and yes, it's very powerful and full-featured.  But this version of Things is right up there - in my opinion, it's better than OmniFocus because of its simplicity and its design - it's so much easier to use and interact with - and that's the key for me with GTD apps - they need to be easy to use, so you use them all the time.  As an example, the Siri add-in makes it really easy to get tasks out of your head and into your "inbox".

For most users (other than power users), this app will do everything you need it to do - get yourself organised, it's well worth the price!  I haven't yet decided whether I'll buy the iPad and Mac versions, but if they're as good as this app, I'll be investing in those too.

It's been a while Cultured Code team, but this has been well worth the wait!

title: Needs a proper web version
body:
I’ve really enjoyed using Things 3 as my main task and reminder app. The interface is clean, simple, and very well designed, and I especially like how easy it is to organize tasks into areas, projects, and headings. It works really well for managing school homework, routines, packing lists, and other personal tasks without feeling cluttered.

One of my biggest frustrations is the lack of a proper web version. As a student, I sometimes need to use a school Chromebook, and being able to quickly add homework from a browser would make Things 3 much more useful. I currently have to put things into another app first and transfer them later, which adds unnecessary friction.

I’d also love more flexibility around web/Chromebook access and perhaps better cross-platform capture options in the future.

Overall, Things 3 is one of the best task managers I’ve used, and I really like its simplicity and organization. A web version would probably make it a 5-star app for me.

title: Sleek, clean look but still miss quite a few features
body:
This brings forth a few most important features:
- easy/quick entry, even for entry of to-do into area or project (due to its sidebar)
- clean look
- less actions/manoeuvres (due to its sidebar)
- multiple tagging for to-do instead of just one context like omnifocus
- comply to simplicity for task app
- link detection. Touch down and hold to open link. I link attachments like images and PDF files on clouds storage, but the bad side is that I have to maintain those attachments in the cloud storage later when to-do is done.

It's still lack of the following features:
- Note entry in Rich Text Format or at least able to attach some images separately within the app, as photo taking is essential and common in our daily activities. Day One allows 10 pictures per entry. OmniFocus permits copy and paste picture into note field. Since this is a to-do app, I suggest it's good to have at least 3 - 5 pictures attachments for each entry. The best is still having attachments stored within the app instead of links.

- Repetitive to-do feature needs some improvements, especially within project. I'll skip the details, since many have already mentioned.

- Smart filtering by tag(s) or text search at sidebar and good to have a header for groups of smart tags/filters.

- Sharing/export is text format only! Should there be more export formats? PDF with images? RTF? CSV? Excel?

Well, it's a very practical and great app overall. Excellent!

title: Super organize your life!
body:

What I really like and enjoy about this app is how smooth everything works and syncs up with all of my apple devices. Creating tasks in the inbox on the fly and sorting them in folders of all kinds. I have a project folder, resource folder and an archive folder. It helps me organized what’s on the burner now , put stuff on the back burner and put things on the side and come back to it so I can keep all my thoughts and to dos all together. If I had to improve the app I would really enjoy it if things could add photos to the todo or project folders. title: Regret Buying.
body:
Things 3 is missing basics that Apple's free Reminders app already has. There are no location-based reminders, no photo attachments, and no shared lists. For a premium-priced app, that's hard to justify.

The Reminders integration is a problem too. Things deletes what was in Reminders instead of working alongside it. Compare that to Mela's grocery lists. Mela stays in sync with Reminders, updating the text and notes inside each reminder without wiping anything out. That's the bar, and Things doesn't come close.

Updates are rare. When they do arrive, they just adapt the app to new hardware layouts. Then nothing else changes until the next device launch.

I've bought every version of this app. I regret investing in Cultured Code.


*UPDATE*

Thank you for the response. I've contacted your team many times. The answer is always some version of "you're using it wrong."

I follow your release notes by RSS. I know the roadmap.

Shared lists, location reminders, photo attachments. Reminders has shared lists for free. Things migration option is a one-time copy. It's not “sync.” These are well documented issues CulturedCode has ignored from its customers. 

This app is so rigid, it’s not a good fit for casual or power users. I've paid for each version, on each device, for years. Things just isn't worth the time spent working around a stale take on GTD.

After spending over a month with Things 3, I've finally found the task manager that works. It has plenty of powerful features and wonderful flexibility and adaptability. But the winning feature is the clean, simple, fresh-looking user interface. Every app designer should take a lesson from Things 3 for how to create an app that decreases cognitive drag. I believe that a high complexity visual experience for in a task manager app (and other apps)  decreases its utility - even creating a barrier to using the app. Things 3 does what a task manager is intended to do - improve my productivity and organization. Many thanks and kudos to these developers.

body:

There are just a few features I'd like to see in future versions - a month view showing appointments and tasks for each day; the ability to create and edit events from within Things rather than having to switch to another app; the ability to swipe from day to day rather than having to leave the Today view and navigate to the Upcoming view; the ability to see the next Action in each project in the Today view so you don't have to do back and forth between Today and Projects.

First, you can’t share with a family member so having a shared family to do list in one app is impossible with this app. The only work around is sharing a log in, which then floods your phone with notifications for someone else’s tasks! Come on, sharing seems like a fundamental function.

Second, say you don’t care about sharing but want an app for your Mac. I mean after all your integrated into this app, why wouldn’t you?! Yeah that’s going to cost you ANOTHER $50. That is absolutely insane and a primary reason I’m abandoning this app and recommending others who are looking for a to do app look elsewhere. 

Great app, lacks basic sharing functionality and is incredibly greedy.

title: Really amazing.
body:
(From my 8 favorite apps review series on Facebook)

This award winning app is the only app I’ve ever taken the risk of buying without a free look. They are so boss, they can just charge straight up for it. $9.99 one-time.

It’s a to-do list that looks deceptively simple. I love the beautiful interface. So clean and simple. A total Apple-look. But tons of power and potential under the hood. I’m still finding more ways almost every day to organize my life with it.

Think of it as a hybrid to-do list and a project organizer. Groceries, to multi step and multi day detailed projects. It is sweet at both ends.

My favorite among many “wow” features is how easy it is to “punt” a to-do that’s undone at the end of the day to: tomorrow, or a future date, or “someday.” 

You can organize things into “Areas” and “Projects,” or just leave some to-do’s hang loose unassigned. Moving, shifting, and re categorizing is dumb-dumb simple.

It gets 5 Stars in my defeat-friction hall of fame.

If you are not totally in love with your list/to-do/project planner… risk the ten bucks on this. I promise, you won’t be disappointed.

Today, yes I am reviewing the app immediately-something I never do, I was not disappointed. In reviewing the app specifications and recognizing it as a one-time charge I downloaded it immediately. author: hughcrt

title: The mighty has fallen
body:
TLDR: find another app. I was a power user with things, but it no longer fits my needs. 

I never thought I’d write this. Things has always been the best. Always the sharpest looking. Always ready for productivity. Always in Apple’s spotlight. But Things has been slowing down…

Today, iOS 26 launched. I woke up hopeful that Things would surprise us by giving us a new feature. Maybe a new UI refresh. Nope. Their update was a barebones update to stay “current”. A glass icon and a glassy like plus button. Wooo thanks! 

I have bought every version of things. The visionOS release was strike one. A full price for a multi year app that just has translucent sidebars? Come on. I messaged the devs many times asking what most of us are asking and needing: attachment support, better markdown (the current setup is insanely stupid), collaboration, or even a refreshed coat of paint to not look like an older app. The responses we get? Thanks for the feedback, we aren’t doing it. 

Today, I’m uninstalling things. This big update from them is a joke. To the other devs who listen and keep the magic of Apple software release day still magical, thank you. To Cultured Code, thanks for the great years ranging all the way back to Things 1. You’ve lost your touch, your magic. I hope you find it again and find joy in your work.

title: UI could be more intuitive
body:
While Things appears to be the most solid to do app, and one I’ve used for years, there is still room for improvement to make it more intuitive. 

I use a lot of recurring reminders, and each time have to look up how to make them recur in the app. I don’t have this issue with any other app, but Things makes it hard to do, there’s no clear way to make a reminder recurring, instead you have go to to one you already created and find the right place to press to make it recurring. If you have a long task name, you cannot easily get to the exact place to click to make a task recurring.

To make this more intuitive, it would be far more helpful if users could make a task recurring upon creation in the same area where we set the time or date reminder. It would make  most sense to then be able to set the reminder to be recurring, but that’s not how it works on the app. 

Please make this easier and more intuitive, as this would greatly improve the user experience.

title: Satisfying to use! I have some ideas
body: I love the flow of the app. It feels really good to use and I like that it isn’t overflowing with complication. One thing that I would love, which may seem a little redundant, would be to have tasks able to be locked until other specific tasks are marked off. Kind of like the checklist feature, except if it could be with other tasks from anywhere.  Like having a “Long Term Goals” Area with something like “Get a job in so and so career”, but it couldn’t be marked off until you marked off “Graduate” under the “School” Area. Sure you can do that without a feature like this, and you can pretty much do that with individual Projects, but it would be cool to see that work across all your Areas and Projects, leading up to one big goal. It would be like different paths are unlocking, and I think it would be distinct enough to act different than Projects themselves. Another example would be a Project to finish reading a book, with Tasks being “Finish chapter one”, “Finish chapter two”, etc. Finishing the book would be the goal of the Project, but what if there was a “Start a book club” Project or Task that only unlocked once you marked off finishing chapter one? I think that would be exciting to open and unlock things like that.

author: Somewhat Appeased User

title: Anxiety reduction magic/life-changing
body:
I rarely write reviews, but wanted to say thank you to the folks who developed this app, enabling me to abandon iOS Reminders app, My giant 300 item to do list with zero organization, and it’s never ending slew of notifications that would become so overwhelming that I would just ignore them, but every morning it would remind me that I had hundreds of things to do, confirming that I sucked at life. PARAGRAPH - THINGS three is designed with efficiency and genius at almost every turn. While I may desire a couple of improvements, I have found in fully migrating to and using the app, why the developers designed things the way they did in most cases. for example, maximum one hour snooze time seemed silly to me, when I was so used to snoozing for one day on Reminders, but this actually prompts me to change the date of the thing (and to file the thing in its appropriate area, project, etc.) PARAGRAPH Or the inbox, made no sense to me at first, as it seemed like an extra today page, but it’s actually a genius solution to default throw things in until I have the time to file the thing (which is so easy and enjoyable to do). i’m not worried about missing anything now. PARAGRAPH  There is one function that I consistently wish was more accessible, and that is moving an item. I wish that that was an icon next to the rest of the icons at the bottom of any Thing, rather than at the bottom of the screen. it chokes my flow every time. PARAGRAPH
I also wish there was a Deadlines tab (along with today, calendar, someday, anytime…). Using a hashtag to access such an important list is just not robust enough for me to rely on/easy to forget it exists. PARAGRAPH
 I absolutely love and even enjoy the experience of cleaning up my Today page once a day, not just taking things off the list, but selectively adding things to the list - is a wonderful and simple functionality. The burden of my procrastination no longer feels as such, and I am absolutely more productive, and more calm, because of this app.

body:
This app is the best task app I’ve found by far. Things 3 is the perfect amount of simple, making it easy to not get stressed by busy UI or complicated task management and creation.

The only gripe I have is that tasks can’t be assigned a time. The integration of the apple calendar is way cool. Being able to see the time on Things is very helpful, but if I could just have that calendar entry act as a task it would be perfect. Tasks such as a doctors visits need an associated time as to not forget, but feel like a chore and need the reward of being checked off for the day.

Lastly, any dev that offers a one time purchase instead of a recurring subscription nightmare, is automatically a good fella in my book. 
Love the app, I’d switch my review to a 5 star if this functionality is ever added.

author: TimmyD253

title: Truly a great app
body:
Everyone says this app is great, and you read every review, and you’re like, "OK, how great can a task manager checklist be?" 

But it’s *really* great. 

I’ve been using this for the past week. It took me a bit to figure out how to organize my tasks and projects around it, but it’s kept me accountable, and I’ve gotten a ton done this week. My mind feels less cluttered (and paradoxically less blank?), and I feel like I go into each day knowing exactly what I need to do. 

The price is kind of steep across my phone, iPad, and computer (~80 bucks), but it seems genuinely worth it, and you can tell that money is going to a thoughtful and motivated crew behind this. Hats off to the developers. It’s very well thought out. 

One suggestion: not everything needs an AI component, and something is refreshing in that this app doesn’t. That said, I feel like AI could help, maybe a little with sanding down some rough edges— especially around, say, having ten tasks for a day and having it be able to sequence them and plot your day out. That side of things is still very manual, but it also seems like a big hill to climb for the developers. Even at a most basic level, being able to populate frequent or common tasks or be able to look at tasks holistically and do something smart with that. What, I’m not sure. But I’m also not a developer.

title: Collaboration
body:
3 things I would like to see added:

2. The ability to move repeating items before the day it’s supposed to repeat. Sometimes I do things early but if it’s scheduled for 2 weeks after completion, I can’t move it forward to show I completed it before it’s supposed to repeat 

Now for my review: 

I love this app!! I use it to keep track of just about EVERYTHING - from household chores, to bills, to events, travel plans, when to water my plants, what I have for dinner each night! I’ve been using this app for about 6 months, Definitely one of the best to do apps in my opinion, and I love the widget so I can see my todo list every time I open my phone. The $9.99 one time payment is so worth it!! One of my favorite features is the “repeat after this many days/weeks once the todo is COMPLETED” rather than just being everyday or every week, because when I miss a day, the todos don’t stack up and it won’t repeat until you complete the task. I also love how it connects to the calendar app, the way it shows up on the todo list looks so nice.

title: Ye old faithful
body:
Things development and new feature updates has been sloooooow. This usually prompts me every year or so to want to try a new app (or dare I say the Apple reminders app). However… every single time I leave, I learn that no one knows how to make a todo list app that I can actually rely on. Most of the other todo apps get the most fundamental features wrong: The tasks are too big so I can only see a few on the same page… repeating reminders disappear (which actually costs me money because I use them for subscription and bill reminders) … no ordering by area… horrible UI decisions for creating and editing tasks … I could go on. 

Things does everything you expect in a todo app and it does it reliably. Yes it doesn’t have location based reminders or shared lists… and I wish it did, but I need my todo app to be an extension of my brain and not a hot mess. 

Through my many attempts to find the next big thing… I always comeback to Things.

title: Haven’t looked for another task app in years
body:
I am a web developer who makes user interfaces for a living, and Things just really nails it. It’s deceptively simple but has so much capability under the hood, without sacrificing intuitiveness and usability. The “press and drag vertically to select multiple tasks” when in multi-task edit mode is one of the most satisfying UX nuggets I’ve seen in over a decade of using iPhones. Love this feature 🤩

My only complaint is the lack of integration with other services. I would prefer a more robust option for integrating with other APIs to automate more of my digital life. 

I would also not mind a web version of Things, but I understand how this would affect the (very fair) pricing model of paying for each instance on each device. It’s been great not having to pay for a subscription!

All in all an excellent app, though. Thanks for the smoothness, and keep up the great work!

author: TaylorPlayer

title: Great app. Feels like it was made by Apple.
body:
Works wonderfully. I’ve never encountered a bug in either this or the desktop app. I use them together to organize all of my college work and I don’t know how I would remember anything without them. In particular, I like how quickly new tasks can be added. On my Mac I can just press a hotkey to create a new task on the fly, from within any app. This lets me capture tasks as quickly and seamlessly as possible before I forget about them.

Things has a good balance between functionality and simplicity. I’m prone to spending too much time tinkering with task tracking apps, to the point where just managing tasks becomes a task in itself. The simplicity of Things helps prevent this and thereby reduces the amount of maintenance required. The easier the system is to maintain, the more likely I am to stick to it.

It takes a little reorienting to start thinking about tasks in a way that harmonizes with Things, but once you get the hang of it, it’s very powerful. It’s nice to not have anything slip through the cracks.
author: Wonderingwhy042

title: Reminder Badge Fatigue - New System Needed
body:
Updated:

I believe the badge system has been useful, but we now need a persistent system to help keep us on track. Things is a great resource, but Intend to forget about what’s due or get distracted and don’t get back to a task that is due at a certain time. 

I’d like to see Things add a persistence reminder with a very loud tone that goes off every 1, 5, or 10 mins. This is a system found in the “Due” app, but I prefer Things’ interface. I would drop Due if Things added this feature of persistent reminders. 

Old Feedback:

I'm super excited to see individual time alerts. The UI is much more refined and concise with internal menus and shortcuts, such as the new drag + add button. I've waited a very long time for this upgrade, but I fear it could have come much earlier; however, the developers needed an all new feel to re-justify the price tag. -1 Star for the last point made.
author: Mind Game

title: Data Security and Encryption Failure
body: I have been with Things since the beginning (7 years?). On three occasions over the last two years I have asked whether Things will modify their data security system to allow for encryption that cannot be decoded by its employees. The response has been “in the future”. Unfortunately the confidential data and metadata that is in my Things database is too important for me to leave it to Cultured Code’s Human Resources policies that limit what people have access to my data. I can no longer wait for the fix. I am today switching to OmniFocus which has full no-knowledge data encryption at rest as part of its platform. I do not like the OmniFocus UI as much as I like Things. However data security is more important to me.

title: Great app, just one suggestion
body:
I’ve been using this app for almost three years and it’s been fantastic, but I do have a suggestion that I think will make this app even better. When you look at your list of to-do’s, the app only lists each out in a single line. This is the case for notifications as well. Sometimes when I write a to-do, it’s over a sentence long and it would be nice to read all of it in one go without having to tap on it to expand it just so I can read it all. 

Any to-do longer than approximately five words is cut off and an ellipses is added to the end. This is even worse when you have a deadline set because it shows that label on the far right side of the to-do, taking up that much extra space. Something as simple as allowing text to use two lines instead of one would be wonderful. Hopefully this can be changed in an update. What inspired me to write this review was how I’d be notified of a to-do and I could complete it right from that banner BUT, I’d still end up opening the app to confirm all what I wrote instead of completing the to-do right from the Notification Center. Other than all of this, it’s a great app.

title: A fix for what wasn’t broken; but good functionality
body:
Update: I was too harsh. I do like some features of Things 3. It’s much easier to move a to do item to a future date. There are still some cosmetic options I would like—lines between items, a graying out of the background for a completed task rather than just the text, keeping the title of the task visible when selecting a new date for it. But overall I like the functionality of Things 3. My opposition to design change for the sake of design change stands. 

I have loved using Things 2 for years. It was the simple, elegant to do list I need. With Things 3, once an item is checked (even accidentally), it disappears—so I am scrambling to undo if I even notice that an item is gone, or at best, I don’t see what I’ve accomplished. I liked to have a blank, checked off item that I could use as a divider between sections of my to do list—no longer possible in Things 3. There are no longer lines between items, so everything appears to have melted into one giant mass of tasks. In a to do list app, I am looking for efficiency. I am not looking for change just for the sake of change and new bells and whistles. Why not just let Things 3 users select the Things 2 interface if they prefer it?

title: Underwhelmed
body:
This has so much potential but shoots itself in the foot for silly reasons. 

Sync Cloud is slow and buggy. What makes this all the more egregious is how their website goes on and on about how perfect it is and how critical it is for it to be transparent and instant. Well, hate to break it to you but it’s neither. Major fail. 

And what’s even MORE egregious is they could and should have just used iCloud sync. How tragic. I read a lot of reviews complaining about the forced upgrade being a money grab due to sync and now I must believe it to be true. 

The software would be worth every single penny they charge for every platform but if only they just saved themselves the trouble and had used iCloud sync. But I guess this would have forbade them the excuse of forcing legacy users to upgrade. Money grab gone wrong. Tragic tragic. 

Next: my calendar can sync into Things. Yay! But it doesn’t show up in the widget. What?!! 🤦🏽‍♂️ You’ve utterly destroyed the utility of calendar import. It’s invisible. It’s not playing a role in my deliverables and schedule for the day as presented by things. 

Next: managing tags is a nightmare. What horrendous usability. I can’t find a single place to easily edit them and organize them. I thought maybe the Mac version would support this but no. It’s even more limited than the iPhone app (which does offer a very hamstrung and clunky UX for tag creation and management). 

Speaking of poor tag management: Things supports creating groups of tags. Sounds great but the implementation is useless and I don’t even understand why this quarter baked idea made it out of R&D not to mention its not at all supported on the Mac version. 

All this just from one hour of using both apps. The promise is huge. No doubt. But the execution at this time is extremely flawed and it seems to me the reason was some bean counter chose to force the team to reinvent the cloud so they could extent leverage and hijack legacy users for money. Quite likely they will end up charging to use their proprietary cloud sync some day to grab even more cash from their locked in user base. 

But the product suffers greatly because resources were allocated on the wrong things.

I’m open to updating my review should they come to their senses.

title: Worth It (?)
body:
Things 3 is expensive.  You have to pay separately (and quite a bit) for the Mac, the iPhone, and the iPad apps.
But they are one-time charges (I suppose until Things 4 is dropped and you want to upgrade). 
Things 3 includes syncing your Apple devices in iCloud.  It appears that this is through a Things (developer) iCloud account, not your personal iCloud account. That’s great but I wonder if the Things business model accounts for “lifetime” syncing for users on the Things  iCloud account based on one-time payments for the apps.
In the end I think it’s worth the investment.  There are a lot of great features.  The to-dos can be organized in two tier groupings: 1) Areas, and then within that, 2) Projects.  Free-form notes can be attached to each tier and the to-dos.  Due dates, reminders, and start dates (if I remember correctly) can be assigned to the to-dos. Items on your Apple calendar can be added to the Things calendar so they show up on Things app today’s to-do (and future date’s) lists. Recurring tasks can be set to recur on successive calendar intervals or a on a set interval after a given task is marked completed.  (Great for things like replacing your furnace filters.) Emails (for example from the Spark email client) can be added as Things to-dos, and a link to the actual email is included so you can read the email from the Things app. The emails are dropped into a Things Inbox and then moved into the appropriate Area/Project grouping.
So far I haven’t found anything missing thing that I’d like or anything that doesn’t work in a way that I think is not OK.

title: Useful, aesthetically pleasing, and utilitarian
body:
Can I call an austere app like this beautiful? Cause it is. It doesn’t have the flashy animations or designs like some of its competitors but the argument is there that Things is more effective at what it does without any of that. I’ve a history of being a bit of a productivity junkie—I believe I’ve tried most, if not all, of Cultured Code’s competitors. Yet after I purchased Things I never went back to any of them.

What animations are present in Things seem to make the app easier to use and aren’t just fluff and filler to distract you. I use this app to run my life. I have ADHD and OCD and without Things I’d probably ricochet through my life more than I am already. If I need to do it, it goes in Things, even if it’s something like “vacuum the floor.” Cultured Code has probably saved my marriage, haha. And the thing is I’m likely not even scratching the surface of what the app can do.

It’s obvious to say that the comprehensive cost for Things on iPhone, iPad, and Mac was hard to swallow. Then again, I’m not paying a monthly fee for the ability to access basic features. I’ll probably balk at the price when Things 4 comes out but end up paying it anyway because I know how much care, love, and dedication the staff at Cultured Code has given Things 3.

title: Rare 5 star review
body:
I am very critical with apps I love and I have to say, after Daylite, Todoist, Omni focus and just about every other task manger app has been tried… I come back to Things and it’s near perfection. It looks amazing, the easy movement and ordering, the way it shows calendar events. The ease of import from reminders app. It’s nearly perfect. I am giving it a perfect score because I have learned to live without the two complaints I have for things (attachments & calendar).
 I understand the implementation of attachments creates a slow and cumbersome apps that would probably wreak havoc on all of the other features I love. So in the occasion I really need an attachment I will just state where it is in the task or notes, hyperlinks take no space, that pdf or image or movie would take a whole bunch.
Regarding calendar, the way it shows linked calendar items in the day view is excellent, it would be amazing if we could touch that area and it had a fully functioning calendar built in, so we did not have to leave the app. But I would venture to guess after all this time there is a reason for this not being there (as then it would be things and dates 😂) but seriously would be a productivity godsend to not have to keep piping between apps for client appointments and tasks, when could be in one place. That being said, it’s still light years beyond anything else on the market for getting things done.

So, is it perfect, nearly ;)
 
Is it the best task manager available. YES!

If you happen to be on a quest for the perfect Task manager …save yourself the years I’ve spent in trial and error and make things your main planner. You will be rewarded with productivity and clarity.

title: For now . . . This is the very best task manager for me.
body:
Things 3 beings a unique approach to task management. As I have worked with many other task managers like Todoist, MS Todo, Toodledo they bring a very straight forward list view interface. Things 3 is different. First, Things 3 allows for tasks to be created and then set aside until such time they can be worked on. This allows for less clutter or distractions. Many reviews see this as a negative with recurring tasks. Once I understood how the product works, it became clear the feature helped me declutter my active tasks.

 

Areas are very well thought out as they play a specific role. Overall if you take your time and set up a system of Areas, Projects and Tasks, you should be able to create a working system that will guide you through your daily work.  The tool is simple yet very intuitive. The tag system is one of the best I worked with.

 

I would like to see custom filters added for more complex views. Sub tasks would be nice, but I am beginning to appreciate the reduction in clutter they create.

 

If you use Craft, Things 3 is the only task manager it integrates with. From Craft, you can simply send tasks to Things 3. It would be great if there was a 2 way sync.

 

The only area I would like to see improved is support. Support is slow to respond. At an investment of $50 - $80 I would have expected a higher level of support.

 

For now . . . This is the very best task manager for me.

title: Recreate Subtasks Manually? Really?!
body:
It’s really absurd that it’s impossible to convert tasks into subtasks. For years I’ve tried to embrace Things into my workflow, but every time I get back to using it I get reminded immediately why I’d never used it for longer than a week before.

If I have any number of tasks 3, 8, 15.. and I decide to convert them into subtasks i.e. group them within a single parent task, there is no way to do so.

It wouldn’t even import subtasks from Reminders!
All reminders subtasks get imported as individual tasks, and I have to manually copy tens of tasks one by one and paste them as tasks one by one.

What an awful and unpleasant experience.

It’s really incredible how such a wonderful and powerful app gets completely crippled by this flaw that renders it unusable to me. I have Things installed on my iPhone, iPad, Mac & Apple Watch. Just sitting pretty collecting digital dust because it’s a productivity nightmare.

I wish the developers would reconsider & deliver this essential feature as an update in a near future. There are paid users like myself that have nought every version of this up & haven’t gotten their money’s worth from the app.

That said, I would pay money to have the ability to collaborate on a to do list with one other person. I don’t need something for a team of people, but rather a way to share a Project with my partner. We are planning a wedding right now and using this app to do it. However, we both wish there was a way to work on the wedding project together aside from sending markup texts back and forth. This feature would benefit so many households without making it into some kind of project management team tool. Please find a way to make this happen!

title: Excellent App but needs critical improvement to avoid being money sink
body:
I would readily pay all $80 the developers want from us for this app suite! It is overall excellent and exactly what I was looking for in a to-do app. However, when I purchase a suite such as this, I assume that I will be able to use it at its current level of functionality for several years -- to put it on the same price level as $30/year subscription services like its peers. When things 3 came out, the developers dropped support for syncing in things 2! This is absolutely unacceptable as if I didn't want syncing I would not pay the extra $30 for the iPhone and iPad apps. I do not expect the developers to maintain expensive servers indefinitely, however. 

The developers need to add support for syncing over iCloud like most other syncing apps on the App store, or my rating will remain low as I expect upon the advent of things 4, sync support will once again be dropped. This would allow users to use the $80 software suite that they paid for for as long as they choose, and purchase the new version if they feel the features so warrant it, not because the developers feel as though it is appropriate to extort users by disrupting their use of the existing software.

title: Still the best task manager
body: Things is elegantly-designed. Though it IS a bit opinionated in how one should manager their tasks (Today, Upcoming), it does provide a structure for folks who need it. The ability to chunk down your multitude of tasks into what you can just do today is very helpful. I prefer flat lists, and I wish that they had the ability to negate the filters (Today, Upcoming, Anytime), but I’ll take it. DO use the free trial on the Mac app to make sure it’s for you, as thankfully all three platforms (iOS, iPadOS, and macOS) work identical, and THAT I can really appreciate. Cultured Code’s attention to detail is second to none. I only wish that the Watch app allowed me to select which filter I want to see, or perhaps only a tag instead of just Today. Minor gripe. If you want or need something a bit more powerful than Apple’s otherwise excellent Reminders, Things may is for you.

title: Excellent task manager that’s close to perfect
body:
I’ve been using Things on my iPhone, iPad and Apple Watch and overall, I have been extremely pleased with the form, UI and sync reliability.

Pros:
I’ve used other task managers that will occasionally stop pushing changes till I spend some time troubleshooting. With Things, this has never been an issue.

Like many have pointed out, the interface and gestures are very sleek and minimal, which makes a fantastic user experience.

Cons:
Although I love my UI to be minimal, I do wish we had an option to show the tags assigned to each task in the Today view, rather than having to type in the search to filter them. Also, I love the idea of calendar integration but it feels too tucked away at the top, I often forget I have events unless I have the calendar app open. And finally, having some method of labeling priority would be perfect! I use the tags at the moment for this, but again, I need to “filter” by tag in order to view them, which then slows down my productivity level.

title: Just get it!
body:
I purchased this on my MacBook and on my iPhone. I was hesitant to purchase because I have bought countless things to help me get organized — planners, calendars, to-do lists, sticky notes, and utilized countless modalities — paper and pen, GoodNotes5, Google Keep, Google Tasks, YOU NAME IT! Nothing has really helped me, and I have probably wasted hundreds of dollars.

Let me start off by saying that I am a very type A person and extremely productive, but I am also obnoxiously busy every day and have ADHD. It is hard for me to focus on what is the most important thing to do to because there’s just so much of it. I am currently a teacher, planning my wedding, I own an apartment building, and have so many other things on my plate. So, when my to-do list gets too long (AKA at about noon everyday), I become completely overwhelmed. I don’t know where to start or how to prioritize.

This app is truly life changing for me. There’s no thrills and it only has what’s important. I can focus on what needs to be done without distractions. It helps me prioritize, I can schedule things out in advance, remind myself of things, organize projects, break difficult tasks into smaller steps, etc. I am SO beyond impressed with these apps and there features, and I am thrilled to have found them to start my year off right!

title: Hate it, hate it, absolutely positively hate it!
body: Where’s that zero star? At $9.99 I can’t find a thing I really like about this clunky bizarrely designed app that makes adding events and todos harder than using the Apple apps. The repeating events are a blistering nightmare to use. How do you better organize your life when you can’t complete a repeating event before it comes due - rather self defeating. It has the clunkiest most irritating repeat I have ever seen. While you are adding a repeat, it changes the due date. Insanity. You can’t just quickly add to Things wo having to go in a double check it’s in the right place, and usually it isn’t. The only thing I can find that this does well is unimportant one time events I don’t need on my calendar or in reminders, like orders I’m waiting for delivery on. In the notes section you can copy and paste in the tracking link and it will open the link with a tap. Other than that, I don’t trust this thing with my important reminders and nothing that repeats. You can also SHOW your phones reminders and calendars, but that’s it, they SHOW in the main app, not on the Home Screen widget, and you still need to open the phone’s calendar or reminders to do anything with them, dumb. I will say it’s not too bad a notes app, but again, it’s rather clunky to use. Plus, the lack of color coding ANYTHING keeps everything blended together. With everything whitish everything on the vertical calendar just blends into a uniform colored scrolling mass and I have to add color dots from the emoji to highlight things, where even if just the tags would color code items, things would be easier to see. I tried using it for due dates on projects, but when you have 3 things due a day from different projects, it’s unnecessarily time consuming trying to find what’s what or what’s coming at you from a project. I don’t like it. I have tried to like it, but every time I try to like it and use it for more stuff, I am reminded what a $9.99 lemon looks like.

title: Simply perfect. Almost…
body:
I have to say that I love this app and don’t know how I’ve survived so long without it. I love the simple concept of typing up a thing you want to do, then assigning it to a day in the future so you don’t have to worry about it until then. Building out projects is a great way to keep track of things as well. I especially love the ability to integrate the Apple Calendar into the app so I can see everything at once. 

I do have one small gripe though. I use this app to keep track of regular monthly bills and when they are coming due. My current system is that I pay forward all the bills that are due before my next paycheck. This ensures I’m always early. However, there’s no way to mark a recurring task as complete before they populate in the Today field. This means I have to keep track of which bills I’ve paid in my head until they come due and I can check them off. It’s very annoying. Other task apps I’ve used allowed me to check them off early, so why not this one?

Unfortunately, this one thing, while small, is so annoying that it affects my overall headspace, so until it’s fixed I can only give it 4 stars.

author: Elle Corona

title: Outstanding user interface but …
body:
Things has the most intuitive and smoothest user interface of any software I’ve used for any purpose in 4 decades of working with computers.  The use of tags, filters, and search is beautifully integrated to make it easy and straightforward to create your own organizing scheme and easily find your tasks and notes as well as having them available for you when and where you need them.  It works very smoothly with the GTD and other methodologies.  

That’s why I use this app routinely in spite of its huge omissions for me.  Primarily, the app is simple not intended for interop. It is only fully functional for MAC users because there is no web or Windows interface or any way to bulk export or backup your data or transfer to other platforms.  That’s a big disappointment for me as a Windows and IOS user.  

My valuable notes and tasks are trapped forever on my IPad.  There is a diagnostic code that lets you grab a snapshot of your data but it’s not in a form any commonly used Zip or MySQL interpreter recognizes.  

I really like the new update that lets you use markdown and nested bullet points for notes, that was another feature set that was missing especially  if you rely on Things for reference as well as tasks.  But the inability to get the data back out of Things is still a tragic flaw from my perspective.

body:
I’ve been using things for several months now but I’m pretty sure I’ve still only scratched the surface of what I can accomplish with it. But that’s totally OK in fact that’s a big part of what makes it awesome. I can get up and running and functioning without having to dig deep into the advanced features. I’m starting to more now and hoping to discover if there are options for shared projects and tasks with other users, which would be ideal to be able to start delegating tasks to my kids as well as letting them see what is on my plate. Time will tell if this is something I can do with this app.

Most importantly though is my current experience as an ADHD single mom of two (one of whom also has ADHD).  We all have apple watches which are amazing accommodations for ADHDers and Things’ integration with Apple Watch is extremely well down.  I also discovered the iOS widget which has also been a game changer.  It’s now the first thing I see when I get bored and swipe open my phone for no reason.

This system is great if you’re a GTDer but even better because it has the flexibility to apply many of the concepts without the rigidity of a strict GTD setup.

Thanks and I look forward to posting an update of how I use Things’ more advance features for an ADHD single mom of two.

The tutorial walked me through learning everything and if I ever need a refresher I can take the tutorial again. I have been using the free version of another to do list but it fell short. Even the paid version didn’t have the ability to make things easy to sort, manage and use. This THINGS App has well organized screen views, the ability to change a task to a project easily and I’m not quite sure how to describe it, but it just flows well and visually makes sense. I have difficulty sorting things out in my head, on paper and with other lists Apps, but the Things drag and drop feature helps to sort, manage and organize easily.  The only drawback is the lack of PC usage. Sometimes it is nice to brain dump by typing with all ten digits. Hope the developers decide to add that functionality someday. Other than that, I say Bravo! I LOVE THIS APP and it has already made me more productive.

title: Great app…fussy standards
body:
Things gets so many, well, things right. It is a dream machine of efficiency and seamlessly gets tasks under control, which makes it difficult to criticize. Not many apps can ring as many productivity bells as Things. And too many task developers just don’t have the savvy wherewithal to blend efficiency with power. 

That said, Cultured Code could stand to lighten up on the design manifest a little and follow some of the top features of their competitors. One being to follow Apple’s lead with Reminders and add actual numbers next to projects and areas on the dashboard page on both their macOS and iOS apps. This allows for a simple at-a-glance check of the number of tasks listed for each project and area that doesn’t involve the needless guesswork of looking at progress pies. Compared with simply seeing a number, progress pies seem like an unnecessary visual trick—more cute than functional. 

Another thing I’d like to see is to partner with other companies that offer very efficient time management apps, like Fantastical. Imagine if Things could have tasks filter in from Fantastical and vice versa. Two great apps that complement each other’s design style and standards. 

I know Things won’t stand still. And they are the tortoise that eventually wins most Apple task app races. I just thought it would be good to make these points now as you crawl ever steadily towards Things 4.

title: My Favorite App - 100% Must Have!
body: I've never rated/reviewed an app before. However when I saw this week's upgrade, I realized I need to let others know how amazing this app truly is. I’ve been using Things 3 for 4+ years (if not longer) and it’s only gotten better over time. Initially I tried many different types of To Do apps but this one did the best at separating my Personal life from my side Business and all the projects those involve. I loved the initial “training” that walked you through how to use Things 3. This app is my life saver…I use it numerous times a day and am constantly adding new things I need to remember to do. I love that it pulls in my Apple calendar events and works with my iPad & Apple Watch. It can be as simple as you want it or as advanced. I’d say mine is pretty in-depth, I have reminders set as far out as 3 years. I work with Drs in my side business and need to keep all their Credentialing up-to-date or they won’t get paid…this app has worked perfect for that. I love how I can plan each day (personal & business all separate) keeping the most important items at the forefront. I also love that I can look to see when I last took care of something, when I started it, who I spoke with, and when I completed it…assuming you write good notes. I used to use the Tags but I’m consist in how I write my ToDo’s and keeping them with their projects, so I don’t anymore but everyone has different “needs”. Since I’m consistent, I’ve always been able to find what I’m looking for when I search. The recent addition of being able to use my Apple Pencil is exciting and I look forward to trying it out. Thank you Things 3 for creating a great app and the continued improvements!

title: Fantastic app, fully searchable and snappy fast!
body:
GREAT APP. I’ve been using it for many years on my iPhone and Mac. It just keeps getting better and better.

The thing that I like the most about this app is that you can SEARCH the entire app for key words, making it very easy to find tasks that you tucked away in projects or folders. The search function is really fast and really great!

I also love that it has a LOGBOOK of all your completed tasks. This is great if you want to look back and see when you called someone or mailed something. You can also search the logbook for key words. I love it and it comes in super handy. Guys, I just looked and I have tasks going back to 2010 in my logbook. Wow, just wow. Thank you Things 3! (And by the way, it was just called Things when I created those tasks!).

There is a NOTE section that you can use for every task and this is great for detailed information. This is also searchable making it easy to find that information from task that you may have completed years ago.

Also, the app opens FAST, pretty much instantaneously making it easy to quickly add a task. This may seem like a no-brainer feature but sadly some apps just don’t do that! The whole app is very snappy, very quick.

It’s relatively INEXPENSIVE for the iPhone and I recommend you start there to see if you like it. The Mac app is more expensive, and for my needs I don’t really need it, but it is convenient.

I highly RECOMMEND this app!

title: It’s worth it!
body: I have tried numerous apps to try to stay on top of what I need to do, reoccurring tasks, upcoming events, and my accomplishments each day. I’ve used free apps, one-time fee apps, and subscription based apps. I end up either deleting them immediately, or I eventually stop using them due to how inefficient they are, or I end up with several apps to cover all my needs. I tried just using a regular physical journal, which I do recommend and I still use; but it doesn’t help me with reoccurring tasks or my incredibly long list of things I need to do for a specific category. An example would be, I have a special needs child who needs specialized schooling and assistance with every day tasks. Getting him the help he needs is covered by various government services but requires numerous steps on my part to get each need of his covered. It would require me to have a large desk planner to have something like this (which is basically a project but a one person, non paid project) planned out on a physical planner; but this app eliminates that necessity. I’m still new to this app, and I’m certain that I’m not using it to its extent, but as of now, it has been the best to-do app I’ve come across; paid or free! I have my fingers crossed that I’ll be able to delete some of my other apps and replace them with Things3!

However... my iPhone is not my only device, and this app is NOT worth the $80(!) it costs to get it on all my devices. $50 for the Mac app, $20 for iPad, AND $10 for the iOS/watchOS version? author: keylan7

title: No universal app, no compelling features in 2020
body:
Things is as useful as it was a decade ago. They make the same app they made then. They haven’t released a universal app, have not innovated very much besides things like a magic button. Things was awesome a decade ago. Now it’s showing signs of stagnation. 

There are developers who are looking modern science regarding how humans navigate and organize tasks, motivation, and what causes an individual to be productive.  Cultured Code seems to be looking at how to add underwhelming features. 

This may be called Things 3, but it sits the category of first-generation task managers. The last time I was impressed by something innovative was version 1. It can’t do cascading tasks, contingencies, doesn’t support calendars besides Apple, very meager NLP, no location triggers.  Not to mention there’s a whole lot a task app can integrate in terms of being mindful of behavioral science. 

In the last couple years I’ve seen new generation of apps that are designed with so much more consideration for what human beings are like. They are still simple and elegant but there is real thoughtful work going into more than just how to put lists in different places. When you use an app like that, Things feels dated. Like they are not moving along with the times, or integrate new information about how to get things done that was not available a decade ago. 

Things was the best, it has a reputation and that’s why folks get it. If you have time to explore new GTD task apps you’ll find there are so many options that are either on the same level, or even more thoughtfully designed for 1/4th of the price. Maybe even 1/10th.  

We are creatures of habit and people that are accustomed to Things will use and recommend it. This does not mean it’s the best. It means it was the best and if you look around you’ll see a lot of options that outshine Things. Options that won’t ask you to pay for 3 apps when a new version is released because they believe in designing universal apps before adding a magic button they want to charge you for 3 times.

If you want to have the most popular product get Things. If you want the best, keep looking. I highly recommend looking for new release apps that integrate habits. Imho, there’s so much intersection between habits and tasks it doesn’t make sense to keep them separated.

title: Meh
body:
I’m disappointed in this app, especially for $10. I have no problem paying for an app when it’s worth it, but this isn’t. This app is based off of the GTD by David Allen, but is missing a bunch of essential parts of the system. 

1. There’s no way to assign a tasks priority 

2. There’s no way to estimate how long a task will take

3. There’s no place to decide what energy level you need to do a particular task

4. There’s no reference area for projects. It would be great to have a reference area where things could be tied to a specific project or task. 

For 1-3, you’d have to make at least 20 individual extra tags for these, which gets messy and isn’t as easy to see at a quick glance.

title: Well-Balanced
body:
Let me start off my saying that I am a business owner that has used this app for 3 years and it took me a good 8-10 months to learn most of the features and how to apply it to my life. Because I am a productivity app junkie, I also try other apps but I keep coming back to this one. 

What makes me search for other apps is the fact that I am a very visual person and would prefer something I can color code that makes it a little more visually appealing. Things 3 prides itself on simplicity, so this is the one aspect I personally don’t like but will deal with because of all the other Pros this app does well.

This app has a really good balance between intuitiveness and simplicity of use. You can add items quickly to the inbox and drag and drop them anywhere. The Plus button is very intuitive as well. I typically use my iPhone to quickly add tasks and view them while I’m out and about, and I use my MacBook for more expansive planning and sorting. The price of these two apps hurt at first, but it’s a one time fee and I have gotten more than my money’s worth over the years.

I have organized and completed many long-term projects using this app, and it’s very helpful for recurring bill reminders. I have a running grocery list that I use all the time. It was also extremely helpful when Quarantine first hit and I needed to keep track of my clients and what I needed to do for them. 

Personally though, most of the time I don’t just go into the app on my own. That would happen no matter what app I have or even if I used a paper and pen planner. The only thing that saves my butt are the reminders, so I have to set well-timed reminders for myself that I won’t ignore. I have gotten more things done with this app than anything else and sometimes I wonder if I’d be more productive with another app - but that part is solely on me because this is a great partner as long as I use all the features it offers.

title: Most Productive I’ve Been In Awhile, however..
body:
After using TickTick for 3 years, I  was wanting to make a change and decided to take the plunge and buy Things 3. A couple weeks later, and I’m so happy I did. I haven’t been this productive and on top of tasks in a long time - maintaining things from small tasks (like email —— back, make dinner, etc). To larger projects that are broken down into small steps. Even seeing the small circle fill up slowly for tasks with projects is satisfying. It’s beautiful, minamilist, and gets out of the for me to throw things into my inbox throughout the day to go through later. 

The only drawback; however, is how Cultured Code currently doesn’t have a web version or Windows app out for Things 3. Of course, I knew this before buying it so I’m not upset by it by any means. But it is the only thing stopping Things 3 from being the ultimate productivity tool across the board for iPhone users who use Windows at work and home. Me and SO many other people would love this and never go to any other task manager app out there if they had this. 
When asked about this they said they aren’t currently working on it, however it hasn’t been ruled out as an option. Other than that, perfect app. 

Thank you Cultured Code and keep up the great work!

title: The best personal task manager on the market.
body:
Things is hands down the best personal task manager on the market. With some pricing model and feature set additions, this could literally put some competitors out of business. Unfortunately I still need alternative software for managing my project teams. Below is what I think could take Things to the next level.

➕Team Collaboration 
➕Timestamped Comments
➕File Attachments
➕Subtask Alerts and Deadlines

Some additional “would like” features:

➕Multiple lines for task titles so they don’t get cut off when longer.
➕Easier access time tags on mobile. Ideally swipe-able like on the desktop app. 
➕Kanban style horizontal view of heading lists on desktop. 
➕More calendar view functionality.
author: bagarwood

title: Everything I need and more
body: As an adult mom with ADHD I struggle to stay organized, keep track of tasks, and easily record important to-dos in an accessible location. The integration this app manages (between watch and phone) is seamless, and gives me a convenient and powerful way to keep track of many ongoing lists, routine tasks, and one-off tasks. I initially balked at the price but this app but its the best money I’ve ever spent on an organizational tool (that’s saying something considering the many bullet journals, planners, tracking systems, etc. that I’ve had false starts with). The tips and hints w/in the app are great, and the app itself does everything I could hope for. If you’re looking for motivational sayings and cute cartoons, this isn’t the app for you. If you’re looking for a way to stay on track and record things as they come to mind- and in a place that you won’t forget about- then I can’t recommend a better tool.
